Base of STA $535F,X in the bitmap-A clear at $B1A1 (X = 248 down to 1): the 21st of its 22 248-byte stretches, the one here, $5360-$5457; $AA filler at the hand-over.

Base of STA $5447,X in the bitmap-A clear at $B1A1 (X = 248 down to 1): the 22nd and last (it overlaps the 21st by 16 bytes) of its 22 248-byte stretches, the one here, $5448-$553F; $AA filler at the hand-over.

Base of LDA $54C8,X at $B134 and $B18A: with X = $78 + row (rows 0-135) it reads the row high-byte table $5540, 120 bytes on. The bytes here are bitmap A's last character row (row 16, from column 25), filler at the hand-over.

Row address table, high bytes: for pixel row y of the 160 by 136 view (y = 0-135), the high byte of 320 * (y div 8) + (y mod 8), the offset of the row's first byte from the bitmap's start ($00-$14). Built by $72A2 at start-up (the hand-over holds $AA filler; $55C8-$55CF stay unused). The drawing code adds the bitmap: ADC $25 or ORA $25 ($40 or $60, the buffer being drawn), ADC or ORA #$40 in the opening, with the carry of ASL for columns 128-159. Read by the octant line routines ($AC68 and the seven like it), the star plotter ($7335, $735A), the planet ($754F, $7566), $AAB7, $AADC, $ADDD, and through the base $54C8 by $B134/$B18A.
Rows 24-87 of the high-byte table. The address is also a base: LDA $5558,X at $B12F and $B185, with X = $78 + row, reads the low-byte table at $55D0.

Row address table, low bytes, for rows 0-135 ($55D0-$5657): (y mod 8) + the low byte of 320 * (y div 8), so eight rows one apart, then a jump of $140 to the next character row. Built with $5540 by $72A2; $5658-$565F unused. Read wherever $5540 is, and through the base $5558 by $B12F/$B185.

Pixel masks for colour %01, one per multicolour column x (0-159): $40, $10, $04, $01 for x mod 4 = 0-3 ($BC48 AND $55, built at $72DE; loader leftovers at the hand-over). ORA $5660,X sets the pixel to the screen matrix's high-nibble colour: the stars (grey on black) at $7366 and $AAE8, and the lines while $AE02 sets the eight octant routines to ORA $5660,X. $ADFC switches them to AND $7760,X, the background colour, instead.

Entries 136-159 of the %01 masks. The address is also the base of the printer's LDA $56E8,Y ($8E39): with Y = token $F0-$F7 it would fetch a word number from $57D8-$57DF. No message in the scripts or the canned table uses those tokens, and $57D8-$57DF are entries 8-15 of the $57D0 table.

Column offsets, one per multicolour column x (0-159): (2x) AND $F8, i.e. 8 * (x div 4), the offset of x's byte from its row's start (built at $72CB). Columns 128-159 wrap to $00-$78: every reader first does ASL on x, so the carry adds the missing 256 to the high byte. Read as LDY $5700,X by the line routines, the stars and $AABE/$ADE4.

Up to 16 points of the current scene (count in $9F), X as floats: mantissa bytes here, exponents at $57B0. $9575-$963C loads them from the scene's data block (pointer $2600/$2700) scaled by 2^-10 ($9610 subtracts $28 from the exponent); every pass $A4B2 rotates them by the heading ($9B-$9E) into $0400/$0440 and $0500/$0540. What the points stand for is not settled; standing at 08-08 three are set.
Exponent bytes of the points' X (see $57A0): bit 0 the sign, bits 2-7 a signed power of two. Written at $9612, read at $A4BF and $A500.

Mantissa bytes of the points' Y (see $57A0), written at $9634, read at $A4D3 and $A514. At the hand-over $57C0-$57FF hold loaded bytes that read like a model's edge list (vertex pairs); play overwrites what it uses.

Exponent bytes of the points' Y, written at $9630, read at $A4D6 (sign flipped with EOR #$01) and $A517. Entries 8-15 ($57D8-$57DF) are also where the printer would find word numbers for tokens $F0-$F7, which no message uses.

The sixteen script variables, $57E0-$57EF. Op 15 sets one (index = operand AND $0F, $8BFE; setting 13 also writes its digits to $BEF9), op 30 copies one to another ($8CE1/$8CED), op 20 can take its message number from one ($8D2A). The scripts use 8, 9, 13, 14 and 15; 8 and 9 hold copies of 14 and 15. Only 13-15 are read by machine code, and nothing but ops 15 and 30 writes them.

Script variable 13, a location number (Y * 16 + X): op 31 compares it with $B7, the current location, and op 26 tests bit 7 of $2B00 indexed by it. Script 7 sets it to 50 ($10E6), square 02-03 where the manual's map has the author's advert, and says THE AUTHOR WON'T LET YOU LEAVE when that bit is set.

Script variable 14, an object number: ops 12 ($941A), 29 ($2940), 32 and 33 ($29C0) act on object [$57EE], and op 20 at $1027 prints canned message [$57EE], the object's name. Set by op 15 (objects 1-46 in the scripts) or restored from variable 8 by op 30; no machine code writes it.
Script variable 15, a value: op 29 compares it with $2940 of object [$57EE], op 19 with $CD; set by op 15 or restored from variable 9. $57F0-$57FF after it: loaded bytes nothing reads.

Logarithms for the game's floating-point maths: round(256 * log2(1 + x/256)) for x = 0-255 (all 256 checked). A number is a mantissa byte m and an exponent byte e, worth (1 + m/256) * 2^(e div 4) with bits 2-7 of e signed and bit 0 of e the sign. Multiply $82FA adds two of these logs, divide $8334 subtracts, square $828B doubles, square root $82A2 halves, and $5900 turns the sum back; the 3D code inlines the same ($9ACD-$9BF7, $A769-$AA38).

Antilogarithms: round(256 * (2^(x/256) - 1)) for x = 0-255 (all checked), the inverse of $5800: the mantissa of a product, quotient, square or root once the log's high part has gone into the exponent.

Sine table, mantissas: sin((x + 0.5) * 90/256 degrees) for x = 0-255 as the game's floats, exponent at $5B00 (checked: within 0.2 per cent). $841F returns the sine of a 10-bit angle (bit 0 of its high byte mirrors the index, bit 1 sets the sign) and $841E, one quadrant on, the cosine; $A544 takes both of the angle $28/$29.
Sine table, exponent bytes for $5A00: $DC (2^-9) at x = 0 rising to $FC below 1, and $00 (1.0, m = 0) from x = 249. ORed with the sign bit at $842B.
The last sine exponent (x = 255). The address is also the base of STA $5BFF,X in the view-colour fill $BB6E (X = 170 down to 1 writes $5C00-$5CA9).

The screen matrix, VIC bank 1: $D018 = $70 or $78 in the view band, $7E in the panel band (characters $7800). Rows 0-16 ($5C00-$5EA7) are the view's colours in multicolour bitmap mode: high nibble for pixel pattern %01, low nibble for %10 (colour RAM gives %11, $D021 the background %00). $BB4F rewrites all 680 with one value when the colours change: $C5 in the opening (grey stars, green planet), $60 OR $A5 from $BB48 in play (blue sky, green ground); loaded as $65. $BB58 compares $5C00 to skip a repaint. Rows 17-24 ($5EA8-$5FE7) are the panel in text mode.
View colours continued (rows 0-16 all hold one value). The address is the base of STA $5CA9,X in the fill at $BB71-$BB77, which writes $5CAA-$5D53 from it.
View colours continued (rows 0-16 all hold one value). The address is the base of STA $5D53,X in the fill at $BB71-$BB77, which writes $5D54-$5DFD from it.
View colours continued (rows 0-16 all hold one value). The address is the base of STA $5DFD,X in the fill at $BB71-$BB77, which writes $5DFE-$5EA7 from it.
A view-colour byte of row 16. The address is the base of the printer's STA $5E8E,X ($8DE3, X = $EA-$FF), which moves the message window $5F79-$5F8E one cell left.
The rest of row 16's view colours. The address is the base of the printer's LDA $5E8F,X ($8DE0), the read side of the same one-cell scroll.
Panel row 17, the first text row ($BA1E switches to text mode at raster line $BA, the end of row 16): 40 solid glyphs $A0, a black bar along the top of the panel.

Panel row 18: the tops of four boxes with titles in the title font (glyph = ASCII - $20): EL at columns 1-4, LOC 7-13, ALT 16-22, SPEED 25-31; the checker $40 between and in columns 32-39. The address is also the base of STA $5ED0,Y at $B66B/$B676, which writes the readout digits a row below.
The E of EL. The address is also the base of STA $5ED2,Y at $B5A0: with Y = $39 the ALT readout's third digit, $5F0B.
The L of EL. Also the base of STA $5ED3,Y at $B598: the ALT readout's fourth digit, $5F0C.
The rest of row 18 from the EL box's top-right corner: the LOC, ALT and SPEED box tops. Also the base of STA $5ED4,Y at $B594: ALT's last digit, $5F0D.

Panel row 19: the EL dial's top glyphs $FC and $FA inside its box; the readouts in figure glyphs (0-9 = $00-$09): LOC at columns 8-12 ('03-00' as loaded, $8D the dash), ALT at 17-21, SPEED at 26-30 with its sign cell $5F12; the COMP box's top with its title at columns 33-38.
The SPEED readout's sign cell: $8B (+) or $8D (-) from bit 0 of $27, the speed's sign, stored at $B5B5; then the four speed digits and the row's end.
Panel row 20: EL glyphs $FD and $FB; the bottoms of the LOC, ALT and SPEED boxes; the compass's tick cells $5F42-$5F45 at columns 34-37.
Compass tick cell 1 of 4. All four always hold the same glyph, $F0-$F7 (the tick pattern shifted 0-7 pixels), stored by $B85D-$B866 and $B8B5-$B8BE as the heading moves; $F4 as loaded.
Compass tick cell 2, written with the other three at $B860 and $B8B8.
Compass tick cell 3 ($B863, $B8BB).
Compass tick cell 4 ($B866, $B8BE), then the COMP box's right side and the checker.
Panel row 21: EL glyphs $FE and $FA; the top of Benson's message box (columns 7-31); the compass's digit strip, glyphs $DC-$DF at columns 34-37, whose bit patterns $B809 scrolls.
Panel row 22: EL glyphs $FF and $FB, the message box's sides around the window $5F78-$5F8E, the COMP box's bottom.

Benson's message window, 23 cells: while a message scrolls in, the printer $8DC3 moves $5F79-$5F8E one cell left each frame and puts the next glyph in $5F8E; $820B blanks it with $A0. Loaded holding MERCENARY centred in the message font (letters ASCII + $80).
The window's last cell, where each new character enters (STA $5F8E at $8DEB); then the box's right side and the COMP box's bottom.
Panel row 23: the bottoms of the EL box (columns 1-4) and the message box (7-31); the checker elsewhere.
Panel row 24: 40 solid glyphs $A0, the black bar under the panel.
The 16 bytes after the screen's 1000 cells, $5FE8-$5FF7: unused ($65 as loaded).
The sprite pointers of the screen at $5C00. Sprite 0's is $D9: its image at $4000 + $D9 * 64 = $7640, the sight. The others ($65, and $AA for sprite 7) are never used: $9374 enables sprite 0 alone.
Sprite 7's pointer, unused. The address is also the base of STA $5FFF,X in the bitmap-B clear at $B1E7 (X = 248 down to 1 writes $6000-$60F7).
Starfield control for the opening, poked by its script (op 25): 0 cruise, 1 accelerate (poked at $706F), $80 decelerate (at $7173). Read at $7415 after each frame's stars.

The opening's event script, one operation a frame from $8AB2, called by the starfield ($7319) and planet ($74F2) loops. It pokes the printer's timing ($E0 = 100, its frame counter; $E1 = 125, the frame at which a message ends), then prints: a title; a countdown; NOVADRIVE ENGAGED; PRESTINIUM ON COURSE; DESTINATION / GAMMA FIVE; DAMAGE CONTROL REPORT; SOME CONFLICT DAMAGE; CHECKING; EMERGENCY; GUIDANCE SYSTEM FAULT; COLLISION COURSE; DISENGAGING NOVADRIVE; UNABLE TO CORRECT; MAXIMUM REVERSE THRUST, driving the stars through $7000 and setting the credits on the way. Messages are literal text ($FF) with bit 7 on the last character; $0D is a dash.

The first message, 23 characters of literal text: ABC UNLIMITED in this crack; the contributor's original Novagen disk reads NOVADRIVE COUNTDOWN at the same place (same length), so the cracker replaced it.
The countdown, with the printer's end frame $E1 = 50: '- 3 -', '- 2 -', '- 1 -', then $E1 = 25 and '- O -' (a letter O).
$7000 = 1: the stars speed up and voice 2's noise starts. Then a call to $0A8F (zero the clock, wait until it reads 2 seconds) and $E1 back to 125.

From the operand of the poke of $E1: NOVADRIVE ENGAGED, then PRESTINIUM ON COURSE. The address is also the base of STA $7077,X in the bitmap-B clear ($B21A): bitmap B, $6000-$753F, covers the whole script in play.
DESTINATION / GAMMA FIVE (the $0D breaks it with a dash).
Canned message 50 (a blank line), DAMAGE CONTROL REPORT, SOME CONFLICT DAMAGE, CHECKING, another blank, and the 2-second wait.
Op 13 sets figure 8, the credits at $7700, to 9000 (operand bytes least significant first: 00 90 00 00): the player's starting money.
EMERGENCY between dashes, GUIDANCE SYSTEM FAULT, COLLISION COURSE, then DISENGAGING NOVADRIVE.
The end of DISENGAGING NOVADRIVE. The address is also the base of STA $716F,X in the bitmap-B clear ($B21D).
$7000 = $80: the stars slow down. Two 2-second waits, UNABLE TO CORRECT, then op 25 pokes $D40B = $81 (voice 2, noise with the gate on: the rumble) and MAXIMUM REVERSE THRUST.
A jump to itself: the script parks here while the stars slow and the planet grows; $7203 points the interpreter at script 0 when play starts.
Unused: $4C and 75 zeros up to the start-up code; nothing refers here.

The game's entry, from the hand-over's JMP $7200 ($5029): JMP $7290, the start-up. The whole of $7200-$75D5 is dead once play starts: bitmap B covers $7200-$753F and the ground-line lists take $7540-$75FF.

Starts play when the opening ends (from $746F): $E5 = 0, $85 = $80; the script pointer $1F/$20 = script 0 (the first word of $0800: the landing script at $086C); ground-line edges 1 and 2 = vertex slots $3C-$3D and $3E-$3F, the current location's own two segments ($8F22 fills those slots); the player at X $08:$88, Y $08:$88 (square 08-08) and height $7F:$00:$88; main-loop branch $A8 = 0, $CD = 0; craft number $A9 = 10 (on foot: $B5DE skips the engine sound for 10), whose 16-byte profile $9D99 copies to $BEA0; $AC = $10, $AA = $40, $AB = $18, $B4 = $3F; the play colours $A3-$A7 from $B27D (white, blue, green, dark grey).

Keeps both grid squares in 0-15, sets the angles: pitch $2B:$2A = $0300 (three quarters of a turn; the opening's descent shows the city from above) and heading $2D:$2C = $0200; then $9950 ($ED and $27 = $88), $B4B2 (no key), $950D (the scene for this location), $9374 (the sight on or off), and JMP $855C, the main loop. Also the base of STA $7267,X in the bitmap-B clear ($B220).

Start-up, once, from $7200. $8135 sets up the machine: banking, VIC bank 1, CIA interrupts off, the raster pair, sprite 0, black border; it also swaps zero page with $BF02-$BFFF and loads the SID. Then the opening's colours $A3-$A6 = $00 $0C $05 $05 from $72F6 (black background), and $BB4F paints the view: screen matrix rows 0-16 = $C5 (grey %01 for the stars, green %10 for the planet), colour RAM green. Then the drawing tables ($72A2, $72C5), the opening script ($72E6) and the starfield ($72FA).

Builds the row address tables for rows 0-135: $55D0 (low) and $5540 (high) = 320 * (y div 8) + (y mod 8). Eight rows one apart (BIT $BBD1, which holds 7, tests the low three bits), then $38 more ($140 in all) for the next character row, the carry going into the high byte, until X = $88.

For each multicolour column x = 0-159: $5700 = (2x) AND $F8, the byte offset (wrapping from 128); $7760 = NOT $BC48[x AND 3], the mask that clears the pixel; $5660 = $BC48[x AND 3] AND $55, its %01 pattern. $BC48 holds $C0 $30 $0C $03.

Points the script interpreter at the opening's script ($1F/$20 = $7001), sets up voice 2 as noise with the gate off (sound $28 through $B93A: frequency high $50, attack/decay $DF, sustain/release $AC) and goes to the star set-up.
The opening's colours, copied to $A3-$A6 at $7293: $00 black background, $0C grey, $05 green, $05 green (the colour-RAM colour).

Starfield set-up: for all 64 star slots, depth exponent $0380 = 1 (a negative depth, so every star is respawned on the first pass), screen position $0680/$06C0 = (1, 1), which the first frame erases, $0780 = 0. Then bitmap A is cleared to 0 (black: $B1A1 with A = 0, X = 248) and the stars are placed ($7370).

One frame of the starfield, looping from $7464: one script operation ($8AB2); a wait for raster line $E0, below the view; every star erased at its old position ($0400 x, $0480 y) by zeroing its whole byte, then plotted at its new one ($0680, $06C0) by ORing the %01 mask: grey on black. Stars 0-20 ($74BF), all in bitmap A (ADC #$40), with no double buffering.
The plot, continued: the pointer's high byte, then the column offset ($5700) and the OR of the %01 mask ($5660). Also the base of STA $735F,X in the bitmap-B clear ($B223).

Moves and projects each star, from $74BF down to 0: its floats X ($0100/$0140), Y ($0180/$02C0) and depth Z ($0340/$0380) into $52-$57; the new screen position becomes the old; Z plus the speed $74C3/$74C4 (negative, $838B); a star whose Z turns negative is respawned ($7472), otherwise x = X/Z + 80 and y = Y/Z + 68 ($8334, $8477), respawned too when outside 160 by 136. Stores the new position and Z.

After the stars, the speed by $7000. 0: unchanged. Positive: voice 2's gate on ($D40B = $81); unless the speed's exponent is $25 (about 512 a frame), multiply it by $74C5/$74C6 (x4.05 the first frame, then x1.012). Negative: gate off ($80); once the exponent is back to $15 (32) the starfield ends ($7467), otherwise the respawn spread narrows and the speed is multiplied by about 0.977 ($7447).

Deceleration, continued: respawn offset $10 (with the mask $1F just set, new stars within -16..+15), then the speed times $74C7/$74C8 through $82FA. The two INCs of $74C9 do nothing: $82FA overwrites A. Also the base of STA $7447,X in the bitmap-B clear ($B226).
End of the starfield: sound $2C on voice 2 (noise, frequency high $30), the planet approach ($74CA), then play ($7203).

Respawns star Y at the far end: X and Y each from three random bytes ($ADEF), the high one masked and offset by $74C0/$74C1 (-32..+31, later -16..+15) and made a float by $8510; Z's mantissa random and its exponent $74C2 ($38: 2^14). Then projects it ($7375).
Index of the last star: $14, so 21 stars (slots 0-20 of the star arrays).
Mask for a new star's X and Y high byte: $3F while cruising and accelerating, $1F once decelerating ($7444).
Subtracted after the mask: $20 (new stars within -32..+31), $10 once decelerating ($7449).
Exponent byte of a new star's depth: $38, 2^14 (its mantissa is random).
The stars' speed, a float added to each depth every frame: mantissa here ($00), exponent at $74C4.
The speed's exponent byte: $15, -32 a frame (bit 0 set: negative). Acceleration stops at $25; deceleration ends the starfield at $15 again.
Accelerating multiplier, mantissa $03 with exponent $74C6: x4.05 on the first frame.
Exponent of the accelerating multiplier, $08, zeroed by $742D after the first frame: x1.012 from then on.
Decelerating multiplier, mantissa $F4 with exponent $74C8 ($FC): x0.977 a frame.
Exponent of the decelerating multiplier, $FC (2^-1).
Stepped by DEC ($7430) and INC ($7452, $7455) and loaded into A before JSR $82FA, which ignores A: it has no effect.

The planet approach: distance D from 1023 down to 0, stepping by $7504[D div 256] (8, 4, 2, 1 as it nears). Each frame: radius = the float $28:$00 (1024) / D ($8510, $8334), a wait for raster line $E0, the disc drawn ($7508) and one script operation. Returns when D goes negative.
Distance step per frame, by the distance's high byte 0-3: 1, 2, 4, 8.

Draws the planet as a filled green disc in bitmap A, centred on pixel (80, 67.5). r squared ($828B) from the radius in X/Y; for each pair of rows moving apart, dy steps by a half (keeping the disc round on double-width pixels) and the half-width w = sqrt(r*r - dy*dy) ($838B, $82A2, $8477), capped at 80. The edge byte gets a partial mask ($75D6/$75DA, %11), then whole $AA bytes (%10) inward (columns $75DE/$75F2), mirrored on both rows and both halves, stopping at the first byte already full: the disc only grows.

Run time: $7540-$757F is the ground-line vertex list, 64 point codes (location numbers Y * 16 + X) filled downward from index $B5 by $8FAE. This byte is slot $3C: the current location's $2D00 byte ($8F2D, read at $90A6).
Run time: vertex slot $3D, the current location's $2C00 byte ($8F27).
Run time: vertex slot $3E, the current location's $2F00 byte ($8F39, read at $90B2).
Run time: vertex slot $3F, the current location's $2E00 byte ($8F33).

Run time: $7580-$75BF holds the first vertex of each ground line, $75C0-$75FF the second: edges 1 to $B6, added by $8FC3 unless already listed, drawn from $908E. At the hand-over: the planet's right edge mask fetch.
Run time: edge 1's first vertex, set to $3C at $7217.

Run time: edge 2's first vertex, $3E ($721F). At the hand-over, from here: the edge bytes ORed into both rows on both sides, then the whole-byte fill inward ($75A3-$75BA) and the step to the next row pair.
Run time: the second vertex of each ground line, $75C0-$75FF, written at $8FF2 and $9022, read at $8FE0 and $9091.
Run time: edge 1's second vertex, $3D ($721B).
Run time: edge 2's second vertex, $3F ($7223). At the hand-over, from here: the next row pair down, dy plus a half ($838B), and the loop back to $751E.
Partial-byte masks for the disc's left edge, by the half-width's two low bits: $00, $03, $0F, $3F (0-3 pixels at the byte's right, pattern %11).
Partial-byte masks for the disc's right edge: $00, $C0, $F0, $FC (0-3 pixels at the byte's left).
Byte offsets of the 20 character columns left of the centre, counted outward: $98 (column 19) down to $00 (column 0).
Byte offsets of the 20 columns right of the centre, from row pointers $A0 bytes on: $00 (column 20) to $98 (column 39).

Run time: $7600-$763F is a per-vertex work byte, 64 entries, saved from $60 at $A948 and reloaded at $9A22 and $9A65 with $0600, $03C0 and $0640. At the hand-over: the last six right-hand planet offsets ($70-$98).

Leftovers from development: $4C 00 00 00, then 12-byte entries of a name (bit 7 on its last character) and a zero-page address: KBCODE( $E9, MYONO ( $EB, POWER ( $EC, ALLFLG( $EE, and OORFLG cut short by the sprite at $7640. The addresses are real: $E9 is the key code ($B2F2), $EB the number of objects carried (at most 10, $9827; stepped at $982B and $990B), $EC set by the speed keys ($B491, $B4AB), $EE set at $80D3 and $900C. Nothing reads the names; in play $A948 overwrites them.

Sprite 0's image (pointer $D9 at $5FF8): one row, $FF $00 $FF, eight pixels, a gap, eight pixels; the rest zero. $8135 expands it both ways and puts it at (160, 116), the middle of the view: a sight. $9374 shows it only while bit 7 of $29E8 (object 40's flags) is set; object 40's name (canned message 40) is SIGHTS.

The scale that the EL dial and the compass both scroll: one byte per pixel row, in 5-row slices, each slice a small digit as clear bits (white holes) in columns 3-7, with a tick in columns 0-1 of its middle row. The digits run 1, 0, 1, 2 ... 9, 8 ... 1, 0, 1 ($7680-$76E8); a '0' slice follows at $76E9. The EL dial feeds it a row at a time into its left column (LDA $7682,Y at $B802, LDA $768B,Y at $B742) and the '0' slice into its right, so its scale reads 10, 00, 10, 20 and on. The compass takes whole slices into glyph $DB or $E0 (LDA $7684,Y at $B878, LDA $768F,Y at $B8D0, ORA #$C0 hiding the tick), a '0' after each.
Tape row 2. The address is the base of the EL dial's top feed, LDA $7682,Y at $B802 (Y = $BC counting down from $5B).
Tape row 4. The base of the compass's left-hand feed, LDA $7684,Y at $B878: the slice ending at Y = $C0 / 2, read upward from its last row.
The tape from row 11. The base of the EL dial's bottom feed, LDA $768B,Y at $B742 (Y = $BC counting up).
The tape from row 15, the '2' slice. The base of the compass's right-hand feed, LDA $768F,Y at $B8D0 (five rows from Y = $C0 / 2).

The dial tape from row 79 to row 95: the last row of the descending 4 slice, then the 3, 2 and 1 slices and the first row of the 0 slice. The EL dial and the compass reach these rows through their feed bases at $7682-$768F, with Y up to $5B.

Inside the last '0' slice. The address is also the base of the sixteen 4-byte BCD figures that script ops 13, 14 and 21 address as $76E0 + 4n (n = operand AND $0F, most significant byte first); the scripts use only n = 8 and 9 ($7700, $7704), and figures 0-7 would overlap this tape.
Tape row. The base of STA $76E1,X at $8CCC, the second byte op 21 stores.
Tape row. The base of STA $76E2,X at $8CD0, op 21's third store into a figure.
Tape row. The base of ADC/STA $76E3,X in ops 13 and 14 ($8C89/$8C8C) and of op 21's reads ($8CB0/$8CB3): a figure's least significant byte, stepping down with X.
The last row of the final '1' slice. The address is the base of LDA $76E8,X (X = 5 down to 1) in both dials ($B713, $B7D3): the '0' slice $76E9-$76ED. $76EE-$76FF: zeros, unused.

Figure 8, the player's credits: four BCD bytes, most significant first. Set to 9000 by the opening ($710C); ops 14 and 21 add to it (a price is taken off by adding its ten's complement, 99995000 for 5000 at $0A29); token $F8 prints it (canned message 17, YOU HAVE ... CREDITS); op 24 at $0E6F tests its top byte.

Figure 9, the sum on offer: set by op 13 before a deal (35,000 to 500,000 in the scripts), added to the credits by op 21 at $1041, printed by token $F9. $7708-$771F, figures 10-15, are never used ($AA filler).

Text for printed figures: token $F8 + k formats figure 8 + k into $7720 + 8k (up to eight digits, leading zeros dropped, bit 7 on the last; digit values 0-9 are the figure glyphs), and the printer reads it as literal text ($8E74-$8EBC). Only the first two slots are used (tokens $F8, $F9).

Masks that clear one multicolour pixel, one per column x (0-159): $3F, $CF, $F3, $FC for x mod 4 = 0-3 (NOT $BC48, built at $72D7). When $ADFC switches the octant routines to AND $7760,X, and at $ADE9, lines are drawn in the background colour %00: white by day, over the blue sky and green ground.

The panel's character set, $7800-$7FFF ($D018 = $7E in the panel band), drawn for a white background: a set bit takes the cell's colour-RAM colour. Several alphabets share it: figures, a title font (ASCII - $20), a message font (letters ASCII + $80) with letters as holes in solid cells, box frame pieces, and the dial glyphs that $B67B-$B8F2 rewrite in play. Here, glyphs $00-$09: the figures 0-9, full-height holes in solid cells, for LOC, ALT and SPEED and the digits in messages.
Glyphs $0A-$0F: the title font's * + , - . / (dark on white).
Glyphs $10-$1F: the title font's digits 0-9 and : ; < = > ? (the ? with a dotted bottom row); none is in the panel layout.

Glyphs $20-$3A: a blank and the title letters A-Z, each with the top of a box frame in rows 0-2 (a dotted line and a solid one) and a 5-row letter below, so a title sits in the box's top edge: EL, LOC, ALT, SPEED, COMP.
Glyphs $3B-$3F: five identical frames crossed by a diagonal stroke; none is in the panel layout.
Glyph $40: the 2 by 2 checker that fills the panel between and around the boxes. Glyphs $41-$5A: plain letters A-Z, dark on white, in no layout found.
Glyphs $5B-$5F: small bar and frame shapes; no user found.
Glyphs $60-$6F: sixteen empty glyphs.
Glyphs $70-$77: a two-pixel vertical bar at eight horizontal positions; no user found.
Glyph $78: a frame with a diagonal (as $3B); $79: an empty frame; $7A-$7F: the EL dial's six glyphs as they are at $FA-$FF when loaded, a copy nothing reads.

Glyphs $80-$89: the reverse figures, digits dark on white, which LOC shows for negative (wasteland) coordinates ($B656 ORs $80 into the digit). Glyphs $8A-$8F: * + , - . / as holes in solid cells: $8B and $8D are SPEED's sign ($B5B5), $8D also LOC's dash and a message's $0D.
Glyphs $90-$9F: small digits 0-9 and : ; < = > ? as holes in solid cells (text bytes $10-$1F with bit 7 set); no user found.
Glyph $A0: a solid cell, the message font's space and the panel's top and bottom bars. Glyphs $A1-$BA: the title letters inverted (frame and all); no user found.
Glyphs $BB-$BF: five identical slanted shapes; no user found.
Glyph $C0: the checker inverted. Glyphs $C1-$DA: the message font's letters A-Z (ASCII + $80), holes in solid cells, as the printer maps them ($8E0D-$8E10).
Rows 6-7 of the inverted checker, then the message letters A-Z. The address is also the base of STA $7E06,X at $B8D5 (X = $FB-$FF), which writes a tape slice into rows 1-5 of glyph $E0, 251 bytes on.

Glyphs $DB-$E0, the compass strip, rewritten in play: $B840-$B852 and $B8E0-$B8F2 shift rows 1-5 of all six one pixel as a 48-pixel strip, and a new slice of the tape enters $DB (left) or $E0 (right). $DC-$DF are on screen (row 21, columns 34-37); here, $DB's row 0.
Glyph $DB from row 1, the compass strip's hidden left end: the base of STA $7ED9,X at $B87D, which writes a tape slice into its rows 1-5.
Glyph $DC, the first visible compass cell (shifted by ROR/ROL $7EE0,X).
Glyph $DD, the second visible compass cell.
Glyph $DE, the third visible compass cell.
Glyph $DF, the fourth visible compass cell.

Glyph $E0, the strip's hidden right end, filled from the tape at $B8D5 and shifted with the rest. Then glyphs $E1-$E4: frames with a diagonal (as $3B); $E5 and $E6 a box's top corners, $E7 and $E8 its bottom corners, $E9 top edge, $EA bottom edge, $EB right side, $EC left side (the corners slant inward); $ED ? $EE ! $EF ' in the message font.
Glyphs $F0-$F7: the compass's tick row, a two-pixel white gap every 8 pixels at eight scroll positions; $B85D/$B8B5 put one of them into all four cells $5F42-$5F45.

Glyph $F8: a slant (as $BB); $F9: a block with a margin. From $7FD0 the EL dial, rewritten as the pitch changes by $B67B-$B808: $FC-$FF its left column (32 rows, $7FE0-$7FFF, where the tape enters), $FA/$FB its right column (16 rows, $7FD0-$7FDF, shown twice).
The last row of $F9. The base of LDA $7FCF,Y at $B7F4, which moves the EL dial's right column down a row.
Glyph $FA, top half of the EL dial's right column (16 rows with $FB), where the '0' slice goes ($B716, $B7D6).
The right column from row 1: the base of LDA $7FD1,Y at $B734, which moves it up a row.
The right column's last row ($FB row 7), copied from row 0 at $B729 and back at $B7E9.
Glyph $FC, the EL dial's left column top row: the tape's new row enters here when it scrolls down ($B805); $B6BC and $B784 write a solid or an empty row here.
The left column from row 1: base of LDA/STA $7FE1,Y in the one-row moves at $B6E4 and $B72E.
Left column, row 2: a base of the row moves at $B6EA-$B6ED.
Left column, row 3: a base of the row moves at $B6F0-$B6F3.
Left column, row 4: a base of the row moves at $B6F6-$B6F9.
Left column, row 5: a base of the row moves at $B6FC-$B704.
Left column, row 11: a base of the downward moves at $B7BC-$B7C4.
Left column, row 12: a base of the downward moves at $B7B6-$B7BF.
Left column, row 13: a base of the downward moves at $B7B0-$B7B9.
Left column, row 14: a base of the downward moves at $B7AA-$B7B3.
Left column, row 15 ($FD row 7): emptied at $B6C4, made solid at $B77C, and a base of the moves at $B7A4.
Glyph $FE, the left column's lower half from row 16: solid or empty rows written at $B6BF/$B787, and the moves at $B6D2, $B7A7.
Left column from row 17: the base of LDA $7FF1,Y at $B70D and of the empty row stored at $B79A.
The left column's last row ($FF row 7): the tape's new row enters here when it scrolls up ($B745); $B6C7 empties it and $B77F makes it solid.

Cartridge-style header (cart = cartridge): $8000 holds $2170, the cold-start vector, and $8002 holds $80C1, the warm-start vector. With the signature CBM80 at $8004 the KERNAL follows them: a hardware RESET jumps through $8000 to $2170, the reset trap, and RESTORE pressed while the KERNAL ROM is in (during a save or load) makes the KERNAL's NMI handler jump through $8002 to resume_warm_start. Novagen's original has the signature; this cracked copy has zeros there (cart_signature_blank), so both vectors are inert. Nothing in the game reads them. Saved and loaded as part of $8000-$803F (save_state_table).

Where the header's signature CBM80 ($C3 $C2 $CD $38 $30) sits in Novagen's original; the crack has five zeros here, so the KERNAL ignores the vectors at $8000 and a RESET goes to BASIC as usual. No instruction in the image stores into $8004-$8008 (every absolute store was searched; the indexed stores from $7FEF-$7FF1 are masked to indexes 0-15).

NMI handler: a bare RTI. hardware_setup points the RAM vector $FFFA at it, so RESTORE does nothing while the game runs with $01 = $35. During a save or load ($01 = $36) the KERNAL ROM's own NMI handler runs instead.

Per-object angle for objects 0-15, in 64ths of a turn (obj = object; xh = the X-height plane): $A6AD turns each model vertex of object $AF in the plane of X ($CF) and height ($D1) by it, through $A728, after the other two turns. Only read (at $A6E1): nothing traced writes it, and it is 0 for all 16 objects in both snapshots. Saved and loaded.

Per-object angle for objects 0-15, in 64ths of a turn (hy = the height-Y plane): $A6AD turns each model vertex in the plane of height ($D1) and Y ($D3) by it, after the heading and before obj_angle_xh. Only read (at $A6CF); 0 for all 16 objects in both snapshots. Saved and loaded.

Per-object heading for objects 0-15, in 64ths of a turn (obj = object): $A6AD turns each model vertex in the ground plane (Y $D3, X $CF) by it first. Boarding object X (key B, on foot, objects 0-7 only) copies it into the player's heading ($988E: $2C:$2D = heading x 16, a 10-bit angle); leaving vehicles 0-8 stores the player's heading back ($98F8: the 10-bit angle / 16). Object 0, the brother-in-law's new ship, holds $20, half a turn.

Binary to BCD table (BCD = binary-coded decimal), 128 entries: entry n is n in BCD for 0-99, and $AA for 100-127, which prints as two asterisks (glyph $0A of the panel's figures) - the ** that LOC shows beyond +-99. Read by the panel readouts at $B662/$B66F (index = the value's magnitude; a negative value is negated first, so -128 would index $80BA, a code byte $A9, and print *9) and by script op 15 at $8C24/$8C2E when it sets $57ED, a location, whose two nibbles it formats into the text at $BEF9-$BEFD.

Resume after a save or load. Reached from $2160 (SEI; JMP $80BA), where JMP ($BFFD) at $8215 lands. $01 = $36, then $B8F6 swaps the zero page back: the game's own $02-$FF, parked in $BF02-$BFFF during the transfer (after a load, as the file had it), returns, and the KERNAL's goes back to $BF02-$BFFF. Falls into resume_warm_start.

Second half of the resume, and the target of the warm-start vector at $8002 (followed by the KERNAL only when CBM80 is at $8004, as in the original): $01 = $36, a fresh stack, hardware_setup_keep_zp, then $D800 = $A6 + 1 so that $BB48, which checks only that first colour cell against $A6, repaints the view's colours on the next pass; $EE = $FF so that the city-map reader at $8EE0 re-patches its operands; then the scene is rebuilt, $9162 (the current room) when the place $CD is non-zero, else $950D (the current city square), and the main loop is entered.
first colour cell != $A6 forces $BB48 to repaint
JSR hardware_setup (with the zero-page swap), then falls into quit_situation. No caller found: its address appears nowhere in memory as bytes, and no traced jump or branch reaches it.

CTRL+Q, quit the situation ($B3F3 jumps here with a fresh stack). scatter_carried_objects spreads what the player has over the city; then the player is put on the surface ($A8 = 0, place $CD = 0) at the same position within a square, the grid square folded into the city (X and Y high bytes AND $0F), height $00:00:80, heading $2C:$2D = $200 and $2A:$2B = $200; $85 = $80 forces the city square to reload; turning step $AC = $10; $9950 sets the speed setting $ED (and $27) to $88; $B270 resets the view colours $A3-$A6 and $C2-$C5 and the sprite colour. The player always gets vehicle 1: $A9 = 1, movement record 1 through $9D99, object 1 taken out of the world ($2941 = $FF). Object 1 stands at 08-08, where the opening messages place the Dominion Dart, with the new ship's model $3B25. Then $9374 (objects here) and the main loop.

Hardware setup, called by the start-up at $7290 (and restart_with_setup): SEI, $01 = $36, $B8F6 (swap zero page $02-$FF with $BF02-$BFFF, clear $0780-$07BF, load all 25 SID registers from $B921: volume 15), then falls into hardware_setup_keep_zp.

Hardware setup without the zero-page swap (zp = zero page; resume_warm_start calls it here): $BB48 (the view's colours), VIC bank 1 ($DD00 = $96), both CIAs' interrupts off and acknowledged, NMI vector $FFFA = $8009, IRQ vector $FFFE = $B9BB, raster compare line 0, sprites in front, raster interrupt on, sprite 0 expanded both ways at (160, 116) in light grey ($D027 = $0F), border black, $B506 (the panel's colour RAM), then $01 = $35 (RAM at $A000 and $E000, I/O at $D000), CLI, CLD.

CTRL+S or CTRL+L, after the digit and RETURN ($B3CE jumps here): hands the machine to the KERNAL. SEI, $01 = $36, raster interrupt off, $B8F6 (the KERNAL's zero page comes back from $BF02-$BFFF, the game's is parked there; SID reset), buffer pointer $FB/$FC = $4000, IOINIT, CINT, $01 = $36 again (BASIC ROM out, so $A000-$BFFF reads RAM), text screen on, SETLFS 1,8,1 (device 8, the disk; nothing rewrites the 8), SETNAM with the 7 characters at save_file_name. save_not_load picks the save ($8218) or the load ($81D8). The file holds 1904 bytes, gathered at $4000-$476F (in the first bitmap) from the 14 regions of save_state_table. Every way out goes through save_load_exit.
device 8: the disk

Load, after the KERNAL LOAD at $81DA (secondary address 1: to the file's own load address; an error, carry set, goes straight to save_load_exit): copy the buffer from $4000 ($FB/$FC) into each region of save_state_table in turn ($FD/$FE, length save_state_table_len + 1), until the table's 0.

Common exit of the save and the load, whether or not they worked: the 23 cells of the message line $5F78-$5F8E get $A0 (a blank), then JMP ($BFFD). $BFFD/$BFFE are the game's own zero-page $FD/$FE, parked there by the swap (after a load, as the file had them). The game keeps $2160 there, so this goes to $2160, SEI; JMP resume_game. A save file with other bytes at that place would send the restart elsewhere.
JMP ($BFFD): the game's own $FD/$FE, parked by the zero-page swap; holds $2160

Save: copy each region of save_state_table in turn into the buffer from $4000, then KERNAL SAVE from $4000 (pointer in $FD/$FE) up to the end in $FB/$FC ($4770); the result is not checked. On to save_load_exit.
The file name for SETNAM: '@0:MER' (the @0: prefix replaces an existing file when saving), followed by the slot digit at save_slot_digit, seven characters in all.
The save slot as an ASCII digit '0'-'9' ($30-$39), the file name's last character: written at $B3AB from the digit key pressed after CTRL+S or CTRL+L.
Save or load: $8D (the CTRL+S key number, stored at $B370) saves, 0 (stored at $B37D for CTRL+L) loads; read at $81D3.

What a save file holds, in order: 14 entries of three bytes (page, low byte, length - 1; read at $81E1 and $8218) and a 0 at $828A. $2B00-$2BFF (location status), $2480-$24FF, $2500-$25FF, $2880-$28FF, $2900-$29FF (object positions, places, lists and flags), $57E0-$57EF (script variables), $7700-$775F (from money figure 8 on), $7ED8-$7F07 and $7FD0-$7FFF (panel character glyphs $DB-$E0 and $FA-$FF), $5EF8-$5F97 (panel rows 19-22), $8000-$803F (cart_header, so the CBM80 signature or its absence travels with a save file, and the object angles), $BDA0-$BDFF (moving objects' lifetimes and velocities), $BEA0-$BEFF (movement record, carried list, counters, flags), $BF00-$BFFF (the game's zero page, parked there). 1904 bytes. This entry's first byte is the page of $2B00.
Second column of save_state_table (read as $8261,X, X stepping by 3): the low byte of each region's start.
Third column of save_state_table (read as $8262,X): each region's length minus one; the column of pages ends with the 0 at $828A.

Float square (fp = floating point, the format described at fp_mul): (X, Y) squared into X and $08 (mantissa), Y and $09 (exponent, sign 0). Doubles the logarithm $5800[m] and the exponent; no overflow check, so an exponent outside -16..15 wraps (2^16 squared gives 2^-32). Within 0.4%. Called by the start-up at $7508 and $7522.

Float square root of the magnitude of (X, Y) (the sign bit is ignored), into X and $08, Y and $09: the exponent's low bit joins the logarithm $5800[m], which is halved; the exponent is halved, rounding down. Within 0.4%. Called by the start-up at $7530.

Unsigned 8 x 8 multiply (umul = unsigned multiply): A x Y, a 16-bit product with the high byte in A and the low byte in Y and $06. Shift and add; $08 and $09 (the float registers) are used as scratch. Called by smul8_q7 and $A24F.

Signed multiply for the object rotations (q7: the product is scaled down by 128): A and Y signed bytes; returns A = the sign times (|A| x (2|Y| mod 256)) >> 8, which is A x Y / 128 truncated toward zero, except that Y = -128 gives 0. Y returns the sign byte A xor Y. With sin64's +-127 values this is a coordinate times a sine. Uses $06, $07. Called four times by $A728.

Float multiply: (X, Y) x ($08, $09), into X and $08, Y and $09. The game's float is two bytes: a mantissa m and an exponent byte whose bits 2-7 are a signed power of two e (-32..31) and bit 0 the sign; the value is +-(1 + m/256) x 2^e, and there is no zero (the smallest values stand for it). The product adds the logarithms from $5800 (256 x log2(1 + m/256)); a carry adds 1 to e; the antilog table $5900 gives the mantissa. Exponents and signs add in one ADC (bit 1 takes the signs' carry and is cleared). Overflow saturates at fp_saturate. Within 0.43%.

Exponent overflow exit of fp_mul and fp_div (taken on the V flag): a result too large becomes +-2^30 (exponent byte $78/$79, mantissa 0), one too small 2^-31 with its sign ($84/$85). fp_add's x + (-x) leaves through $832C and $8328 too.

Float divide: ($08, $09) / (X, Y), into X and $08, Y and $09, in fp_mul's format: subtracts the logarithms ($5800) and the exponents; a borrow takes 1 from the exponent; the sign is the exclusive or (bit 1 is set first as a guard for the signs' borrow). Saturates like fp_mul. Within 0.43%. $A544 uses it for the tangent and cotangent of the view angles.

Float add: (X, Y) + ($08, $09), into X and $08, Y and $09 (callers subtract by flipping an operand's sign bit first, as at $9C91 and $AA05). The smaller operand's mantissa, its leading 1 restored, is shifted right by the exponent difference d through a jump into a run of LSRs (branch operands fp_add_shift_a/b rewritten per call); d of 9 or more returns the larger operand unchanged. Like signs add (a carry raises the exponent unchecked, so 2^31 + 2^31 wraps to 2^-32); unlike signs subtract and renormalise at $83D5. Equal magnitudes of opposite sign give 2^(e-9), the format's stand-in for zero. Truncates: error within 0.55% of the larger operand.

Operand of the BNE at $83AA, rewritten at $83A3 with 15 - d when (X, Y) is the larger operand by d = 1-8: the branch lands d - 1 LSRs before $83BA, so the smaller mantissa is shifted right d times in all (the NOPs at $83AC-$83B2 are never reached).
fp_add's renormalising exit after a subtraction: shifts the difference left until its leading 1 falls out, takes the shift count off the exponent, and underflows to 2^-31 ($84) through $83EC.
Operand of the BNE at $8403, rewritten at $83FD with (-d) AND 7 when ($08, $09) is the larger operand by d = 1-8: lands d - 1 LSRs before $840C, a shift of d in all.

Cosine of a 10-bit angle, as a float: the angle is Y (its low two bits, the quadrant) x 256 + X, in 1024ths of a turn; returns X = mantissa, Y = exponent and sign, the value cos((angle + 0.5) x 360/1024 degrees) within 0.001. Looks up the quarter wave at $5A00 (mantissa) and $5B00 (exponent), reflected and signed by quadrant. Called by $A544 for the view angles.
Sine of the same 10-bit angle (Y:X): entered one byte into fp_cos10, skipping its INY, it computes cos(angle - 90 degrees), the sine.
Sine and cosine of A in 64ths of a turn, as signed bytes scaled by 127: $BEBE = sin, $BEBF = cos. Called by the object rotation $A728.
127 x cos(A x 360/64 degrees) as a signed byte: adds a quarter turn (16) and falls into sin64.
127 x sin(A x 360/64 degrees) as a signed byte (A taken mod 64), from the half wave sine64_table, negated for the second half; Y returns A AND 63.
Half a sine wave, 32 bytes: round(127 x sin(n x 360/64 degrees)) for n = 0-31 (0, 12, 25, ... 127 at n = 16 ... 12). Read by sin64 at $844B.

Float (X, Y) to a signed byte in A, rounded to nearest (halves away from zero), carry clear; carry set when the magnitude is 127.5 or more (A then not valid). The shift count goes into the BNE operand fp_to_int8_shift.
Operand of the BNE at $8486, rewritten at $8480 with the exponent e (0-6): skips e of the seven LSRs, so the mantissa with its leading 1 is shifted right 8 - e times in all.

Float (X, Y) to a signed 16-bit integer, X = high byte, Y = low byte: the magnitude truncated, and for a negative value its ones' complement, -trunc(|x|) - 1 (the floor, except that an exact integer comes out one lower). Magnitudes below 1 give 0, or -1 if negative. Carry set when e is 15 or more (32768 or more). The shift count goes into the BCC operand fp_to_int16_shift. fire_missile uses it for the missile's velocity.
Operand of the BCC at $84C1, rewritten at $84B5 with 3e: skips e of the fifteen three-byte LSR/ROR pairs, a right shift of 16 - e in all.

Signed 24-bit integer (A = high, X = middle, $07 = low) to a float, returned as A = $08 = mantissa and X = $09 = exponent and sign (A and X, not X and Y). Negates a negative number, finds the leading 1 and keeps the 8 bits after it (truncating, within 0.4%). Zero gives 2^-8 (mantissa 0, exponent byte $E0). Turns 24-bit position differences (object or vertex minus the player) into floats for the view ($A5CE, $A635).

Main loop, one pass per view redraw (10 passes in 100 frames standing on the ground). Every pass: $8AB2 runs one event-script operation; hired_ship_update. Then $A8 picks the branch: 0 is the surface (main_loop_surface), non-zero is inside a complex. Inside: $A544 (sines, cosines, tangents of the view angles), $AF6E (wait for raster line $E0, swap the double buffer); then $939E keeps the player inside the room's walls, and on touching one (with the door delay $B1 at 0) $9437 looks for a door there and $90BE goes through it, into room $08, or to the surface when that is 0 (the pass then goes on at $85B0), setting $B1 = 2; $96D8 (the room's vertices), $AE02, $96E7 (its edges), $ADFC, $9706 (the objects here, keys T and B), $B2FE (joystick), $A165 (movement), and round.

Main loop, surface branch ($A8 = 0): $A544 (view angles), $94E0 (reload the city square when the player's square changes), $A320 (in a vehicle, or when $CA is set), $A4B2, $AF6E (buffer swap); from $85B0, also the way in from a door out of a complex: $9054, and the building of the player's square ($B7 not 0) through $96D8/$96E7 when the player is low (height high byte $77 = 0) or $CA is set; object 0, the brother-in-law's new ship, moves one step along Y ($2500 + 1 a pass, high byte $25C0 wrapping 15 to 0); $ADFC, $9706 (objects), $B2FE, $A165 (movement), fire_missile with A = $30, building_hit_update, move_objects, attack_ship_update, and round.
object 0 (the new ship) moves along Y

Scatter what the player has (quit_situation): the vehicle the player is in ($A9, when positive) and every carried object (the list $BEB1 onward, $EB of them, top first) is put on the surface ($2940 = 0) in a random square of the city: X and Y high bytes random 0-15, middle bytes random ($ADEF), low bytes kept, height 0; its carried bit ($29C0 bit 7) is cleared. Leaves $EB = 0.

The hired ship (object 7), every pass. $BEFF = 0: nothing. Negative (script 2 pokes $FF after 'SHIP DESPATCHED / IT WILL LAND AT LOC 8-8 IN 2 MINS'): object 7 is put on the surface ($2947 = 0) at X $08:$99:$00, Y $08:$8B:$00, height $7F:$00:$00, and $BEFF = $7F. Positive: the height (high:middle bytes) loses height/128 + 1 a pass until it is exactly 0, then $BEFF = 0. The descent takes 780 passes (about 2.6 minutes at the 5 passes a second measured on the ground).

Moving objects 8-15 (8 the player's missile, 14 the attack ship's missile, 15 the attack ship), every surface pass. A lifetime at $BDA3,X ($BDAB-$BDB2) counts down; 0 and $7F leave the object alone; reaching 0 calls remove_object and ends the pass's loop. Otherwise the 24-bit X, height and Y get the velocities $BDAB/$BDB3/$BDBB,X, $BDC3/$BDCB/$BDD3,X and $BDDB/$BDE3/$BDEB,X added; a height gone negative is set to -1 ($FF:$FF:$FF). Object 8, the last, goes on to missile_collisions.
Take object X out of the world: place $2940,X = $FF, lifetime $BDA3,X = 0, then $9374 rebuilds the list of objects present.

The player's missile (object 8) after its move. Low (height below $00:$08:$00, or below the ground) near the centre of a city square (X and Y middle bytes $70-$8F, inside the city): it hits the building there: $F5 = the square's index, $FB = its status byte before, bit 7 (destroyed) set in $2B00,Y, explosion countdown $F4 = 16, sound 4, the missile removed, and building_hit_update's first step. Below the ground elsewhere: removed. Otherwise it is tested against object 15, the attack ship (a hit prints canned message $31, ENEMY SHIP DESTROYED), and object 0, the brother-in-law's new ship (a hit starts script 27, which names it).
bit 7: the building at this square is destroyed

After a building hit ($F4 counting down): nothing unless the player is in the hit square ($B7 = $F5). With the ANTI TIME BOMB carried (object 24, $29D8 bit 7) the square's status goes back to its value before the hit without the destroyed bit: a building already destroyed has its square reloaded ($9575), standing again, and its debris finished at once. Otherwise it waits for the debris ($96AC) and the countdown; then, if the building was intact before and its status lacks bit 5, the side's count goes up: bit 6 set (the Mechanoid squares) in $BEBC, clear (the Palyar squares) in $BEBB; bit 5 marks nobody's squares (the Metal Detector at $B53D shows these bits as red, blue and green). $BEBC - $BEBB reaching 105 starts script 10 (the Palyars: a reward in the red hangar), $BEBB leading by 106 script 26 (the Mechanoids); otherwise the square's own script 32 + (bits 0-4) starts, once (the bits are cleared).

Is object Y, on the surface ($2940,Y = 0), within 4/256 of a square of object X on every axis (object_difference, then $999A with 4)? Carry clear if so: sound $10, the attack is called off ($BEF8 = 0), object Y's lifetime is zeroed (unless Y = 0) and it leaves the world ($2940,Y = $FF), and object X is removed. X and Y are kept.

Fire, every surface pass (A = $30 from the main loop). Only when fire is pressed ($81 = 0), the player is in a vehicle ($A9 positive), no explosion runs ($F4 = 0) and missile object 8 is idle (lifetime $BDAB = 0): sound 8, object 8 into the current place $CD at the player's position with lifetime 16, and a velocity along the view direction, the floats $4C/$4D (X: cos a2 x sin a3), $36/$37 (height: sin a2), $50/$51 (Y: cos a2 x cos a3), a2 = $2A:$2B and a3 = $2C:$2D (heading), with A added to each exponent byte ($30 is 12 powers of two: 4096 units, 1/16 of a square a pass), through fp_to_int16 and sign-extended into $BDB3/$BDBB/$BDC3, $BDCB/$BDD3/$BDDB and $BDE3/$BDEB/$BDF3. $9374 rebuilds the object list.

The attack ship (object 15) and its missile (object 14), every surface pass while $BEF8 is set (the scripts of destroyed buildings set it: 34 and 35 at random, the landmarks' and the new ship's always) and $CA is 0. Farther than $30/256 of a square on some axis: the ship homes, velocity (player - ship)/32, lifetime $AD. Nearer: if object 14 is idle it is launched from the ship with velocity (player - ship)/16 and lifetime 32; if it is in flight and within 4/256 of the player on every axis the player is hit: $B22D (view colours $11, sound $18), canned message $30 SHIP DESTROYED when in a vehicle, the attack ends ($BEF8 = 0), sound $0C, movement mode 9 ($A9 = 9, $9D99), ship and missile removed.

Divide the three 24-bit differences $D5-$D7 (X), $D8-$DA (height), $DB-$DD (Y) by 2^Y (arithmetic shifts right, Y times), then complement all nine bytes: -(d >> Y) - 1, turning object - player into a step toward the player.
Copy object Y's 24-bit position (the nine split tables $2880/$2480/$2540, $28C0/$24C0/$2580, $2900/$2500/$25C0) to object X.
Store the nine bytes $D5-$DD as object X's velocity: $BDAB/$BDB3/$BDBB,X (X), $BDC3/$BDCB/$BDD3,X (height), $BDDB/$BDE3/$BDEB,X (Y).
24-bit position of object X minus that of object Y, per axis, into $D5-$D7 (X), $D8-$DA (height), $DB-$DD (Y); the counterpart of $9957, which subtracts the player's position.

Start event script A from machine code (the missile and building code, $921E, $98C0): ignored while $BEC0 bit 6 is set (one such script at a time); otherwise sets it, pushes the running script's pointer $1F/$20 on the script stack ($8BC9, $BEC2) and points $1F/$20 at script A from the table $0800. The scripts clear bit 6 when they finish.

Script step: the event-script interpreter, one operation per call, from the main loop $855C and the opening sequence's loops ($7319, $74F2, $AA95). Returns at once while a message is printing ($E6 non-zero), so every script waits for Benson to finish. Otherwise it reads the operation byte at the script pointer ($1F),0 into $E7 (bit 7 inverts a test, bit 6 makes a taken test a call), writes $8D5E + 2 x (op AND $3F) into the pointer of the JMP ($8D5E) at $8ACC and so jumps to that operation's handler. Handlers read their operands through ($1F),Y and finish at $8B92 (move $1F/$20 past the operation) or $8BB2 (move it to a target).
pointer patched: $8D5E + 2 x op
Script dispatch, low byte: the pointer operand of JMP ($8D5E) at $8ACC, rewritten on every step by $8AC2 with $5E + 2 x op, so that the jump reads the handler's address out of the table $8D5E.

Script dispatch, high byte of the same pointer: $8D plus the carry out of the low byte, written by $8AC9; it is always $8D, since even op $3F gives $5E + $7E, below $100 (ops 35-63 would read past the table into the code at $8DA4).

Script op 24, if peek: operands a memory address (low, high) and a value, then the two-byte target. Writes the address into the CMP at $8ADF ($8AE0/$8AE1) and compares the value with the byte found there: the branch is taken when that byte is greater than the value, or, with bit 7 of the op, when it is not. Its one use, at $0E6F, tests $7700 > 0, credits of 1,000,000 or more, before the 999,999-credit ship hire.
address patched by $8AD3/$8AD9; $0100 is a placeholder
Op 24's address, low byte: the operand of CMP $0100 at $8ADF, written from the script by $8AD3.
Op 24's address, high byte, written by $8AD9; the $0100 in the snapshot is only a placeholder.

Script op 10, if random: one operand, then the target. Steps the random generator $ADEF and branches when the operand is below the new random byte $E8, or, with bit 7, when $E8 is at most the operand. The scripts use it inverted with operand $50, taken for 81 values of 256 ($0A74, $0CD4, $0CDB).

Script op 7, if clock: a number of seconds (low, high), then the target. Reads the seconds clock $E3 (low) and $E4 (high), again if $E3 changed between the reads (the panel interrupt counts it), and branches while the clock is below the number; bit 7 branches once it has reached it. With op 2 it makes the scripts' waits: $0A8F clears the clock and loops on op 7 for two seconds.

Script op 23: one operand, then the target. Branches when the signed byte $BEBD is below the operand minus 128 (it compares $BEBD EOR $80 with the operand, unsigned); bit 7 inverts. No script in this image uses it, and op 22 is the only other code that touches $BEBD.

Script op 34, if craft: one operand, then the target. Branches when $A9, the number of the object the player is riding ($80 on foot, $98E2), equals the operand. Script 0 waits at $09BB for 1, the Dart; script 7 tests 7, the interstellar ship ($1096, $10D3).

Script op 29, no operands, then the target: branches when object $57EE lies in room $57EF ($2940 + object holds the room an object is in, 0 outdoors, $FF while carried). $0E0C: the Antenna (30) in the Communication Room ($10).

Script op 19, no operands, then the target: branches when the player is in room $57EF, compared with the current room $CD (0 outdoors). The briefings run it inverted ($0CF1, $0DC7) to stop when the player walks out.
Script op 18, if flags: a mask, then the target. Branches when any bit of the mask is set in the script flags $BEC0 (bit 7 of the op inverts).

Script op 12, if carried: no operands, then the target. Branches when object $57EE is in the player's carried list $BEB1 ($941A). The Communication Room ($0E0F) and the interstellar ship ($10A4) look for the Antenna and the Novadrive this way.
Script op 9: a machine-code address (low, high), then the target. Calls it through $8C5D and branches when it comes back with the carry clear. No script in this image uses it (see $8C5D).
Script op 6: a grid X and a grid Y, then the target. Branches when the player's square, $74 and $7A, is that one (underground both are 0). No script in this image uses it.

Script op 31, no operands, then the target: branches when variable $57ED equals $B7, the location number of the player's square (Y x 16 + X, 0 outside the city, set at $952B). No script in this image uses it.

Script op 11, if key: a key number, then the target. When the last key $E9, SHIFT and CTRL bits dropped, equals the operand, it forgets the key ($B4B2), calls $B94D (sound 0 on voice 1) and branches; otherwise it goes on. The scripts poll it in a loop against the clock: Y ($19) at $0AB6 (buy, hire) and $10CF (launch).

Script op 26, no operands, then the target: branches when bit 7 of $2B00 + $57ED is set, the building at location $57ED destroyed. The escape at $10E6 sets $57ED to $32 (02-03, the author's advert) and will not leave while it is.

Script op 33: a mask, then the target. Branches when any bit of the mask is set in object $57EE's flags $29C0 (bit 0 sold, 2 starts the object's script and 3 prints its name when it is taken or boarded ($98B1), 4 cannot be taken, 5 too heavy without the Antigrav, 7 carried). The shops test bit 0 at $1010.

Script test tail, shared by every test: enter at $8B87 when the condition is false, at $8B8A when true, or at $8B8B with the carry clear for true. The carry goes into bit 7 and bit 7 of the op ($E7) inverts it. Not taken: the pointer moves past the two-byte target to the next operation ($8B90). Taken: $8B9E jumps to the target, or calls it when bit 6 of the op is set ($8BA3). $8B92 is also where the other operations end: $1F/$20 += Y + 1, Y being the index of their last operand.

Script op 4, call: a two-byte target. Pushes the address of this operation + 3 on the script stack (low, then high, $8BC9) and jumps. A taken test with bit 6 set enters here too and pushes the same + 3, which is right only for op 4; no script in this image sets bit 6.
Script op 3, jump: loads the script pointer $1F/$20 with the two-byte target. Every taken test ends here.
Script op 5, return: pops the script pointer from the script stack ($8BD2: the high byte, then the low).

Script stack push: stores A at $BEC2 + $E5 and raises the index $E5. The stack holds the return addresses of script calls ($8BA3) and of scripts started as calls by $8A8C; $7203 empties it at start-up.
Script stack pop: lowers $E5 and returns the byte at $BEC2 + $E5 in A.

Script op 32: one mask for object $57EE's flags $29C0. Below $80 it sets the mask's bits; $80 and above it ANDs the flags with the mask, clearing the bits that are 0 in it. Bit 7 (carried) cannot change either way. The shops set $11 at $1039: sold (bit 0) and no longer takeable (bit 4).

Script op 15, set variable: a variable number (low nibble) and a value for $57E0 + n. The scripts use $57EE for an object number, $57EF for a room number and $57ED for a location number (Y x 16 + X). Setting $57ED also writes that location as the word 'XX-YY' at $BEF9-$BEFD (dictionary word $CB, digits by $8C23), which no message in this image prints.

Location digits: writes the two decimal digits of X (0-15), from the BCD table $803A, at $BEF9 + Y and $BEFA + Y and returns with Y + 1. The second character is the whole BCD byte, so 10-15 give $10-$15, which the printer shows as glyphs $90-$95, digits of another style than the figures $00-$09.

Script op 1, print: the message tokens that follow, up to a 0. Points the printer's token read (the operand $8E27/$8E28 of the LDY at $8E26) at this operation, whose first token is one byte on, skips the tokens and starts the printer: $E6 = $FF, token index $DE and character index $DF = 0. The next step then waits until the message has been shown.
Script op 2, clock reset: zeroes the seconds clock $E3-$E4, the start of every timed wait (op 7).
Script op 8: calls the machine code at the two-byte address that follows ($8C5D), then goes on. No script in this image uses it.

Calls the machine code whose address (low, high) follows in the script, by writing it into the JSR at $8C69. That JSR comes back to $8C6C, op 13's handler, so a routine ending in a plain RTS would go on to run op 13 on the script's next bytes; only one that drops its own return address would return cleanly. Ops 8 and 9, its only callers, are unused in this image.
The JSR that ops 8 and 9 aim, by rewriting its operand $8C6A/$8C6B; in the snapshot it points at itself.
target patched by $8C60/$8C66
Low byte of the machine-code address that ops 8 and 9 call, written by $8C60.
High byte of the machine-code address that ops 8 and 9 call, written by $8C66.

Script op 13, set counter: a counter number n (low nibble) and four BCD bytes, least significant first, stored at $76E3 + 4n down to $76E0 + 4n: a counter is big-endian in memory. It shares op 14's loop, first turning the ADC $76E3,X at $8C89 into BIT $76E3 so that the loop stores instead of adding. The intro sets counter 8, the credits, to 9000 ($710C); the shops set counter 9, the reward on offer.

Script op 14, add to counter: counter n and four BCD bytes, least significant first, added in decimal mode; the carry out of the top byte is lost. Puts the ADC back at $8C89. There is no subtraction: $0A29 adds 99995000 to take 5000 credits for the Dart, $0E90 adds 99000001 to take 999999 for the Hertz ship.
Opcode of the counter loop's ADC $76E3,X: op 13 writes $2C (BIT $76E3, so the loop stores the script's bytes) and op 14 writes back $7D (ADC).
opcode patched: ADC (op 14) or BIT (op 13)
Script op 21, sum counters: three counter numbers a, b, c (low nibbles): counter c = counter a + counter b in BCD, the carry out lost. Used once, at $1041: credits (8) = reward (9) + credits (8).
Script op 30, copy variable: one byte, the destination in the high nibble and the source in the low: $57E0 + high = $57E0 + low. $104C-$105B save and restore $57EE/$57EF in $57E8/$57E9 this way.

Script op 16, set flags: ORs its operand into the script flags $BEC0, which ops 17 and 18 clear and test. The scripts use bit 0 for a yes answer ($0AC2), 1 for opposition sites destroyed ($11F5), 2 for the ship despatched ($0EBE), 3 for the author's advert destroyed ($0B6B) and 5 for the brother-in-law offended ($0A67).
Script op 17, clear flags: clears the bits of its operand in $BEC0. Scripts started as calls end with it on bit 6 ($40), the busy bit that $8A8C sets and checks before it starts another.

Script op 25, poke: an address (low, high) and a value, stored there by the STA at $8D1C, whose operand ($8D1D/$8D1E) it rewrites. The scripts poke the printer's timers $E0/$E1, SID voices 1 and 2 ($D404, $D40B), $7000, $296E and $BEF8, $BEFE, $BEFF.
address patched by $8D10/$8D16; $0100 is a placeholder
Op 25's address, low byte: the operand of STA $0100 at $8D1C, written by $8D10.
Op 25's address, high byte, written by $8D16; the snapshot's $0100 is only a placeholder.

Script op 20, message: a canned message number (0-63); with bit 7 set the number is read from variable $57E0 + (low nibble). Starts it through $8DAA. A number above 63 is not checked and would read past the 64-entry pointer tables.

Script op 27, random message: a mask and a base; starts canned message (random AND mask) + base ($ADEF, then $8DAA). Used once, at $08B7: one of messages 60-63 after the crash (WHERE AM I, YOU CRASHED, GOOD LANDING!, OUCH!). A sum of 0 would fall into op 28 instead and print nothing.
Script op 28, clear key: forgets the last key ($B4B2 stores $04 in $E9), so that a following key test needs a fresh press; used before the yes/no questions ($0AAB, $0E4C, $10B9).
Script op 22: adds its signed operand to $BEBD, saturating at -128 ($80) and +127 ($7F) instead of wrapping. No script in this image uses it, nor op 23, the only other code that touches $BEBD.
A spare $00 byte between op 22's handler and the handler table: the dispatch indexes from $8D5E, and no instruction reads it.

Script handlers: 35 addresses indexed by operation number (op AND $3F), read by the JMP ($8D5E) at $8ACC. Entry 0, here, is $0000: no script uses op 0, which would jump to $0000. Ops 1-34 follow at $8D60.
entry 0 = $0000: no op 0

Script handler addresses for ops 1-34: 1 print $8C36, 2 clock reset $8C4E, 3 jump $8BB2, 4 call $8BA3, 5 return $8BBE, 6 if square $8B47, 7 if clock $8AF0, 8 call code $8C57, 9 if code $8B41, 10 if random $8AE5, 11 if key $8B60, 12 if carried $8B37, 13 set counter $8C6C, 14 add to counter $8C73, 15 set variable $8BF5, 16 set flags $8CF3, 17 clear flags $8CFF, 18 if flags $8B2D, 19 if player in room $8B24, 20 message $8D22, 21 sum counters $8C98, 22 add to $BEBD $8D46, 23 if $BEBD below $8B03, 24 if peek $8AD0, 25 poke $8D0D, 26 if destroyed $8B72, 27 random message $8D34, 28 clear key $8D40, 29 if object in room $8B17, 30 copy variable $8CDB, 31 if at location $8B57, 32 object flags $8BDB, 33 if object flags $8B7C, 34 if craft $8B0E. Ops 6, 8, 9, 22, 23 and 31 appear in no script of this image.

op 2: clock reset
op 3: jump

op 7: if clock
op 8: call code (unused)
op 9: if code (unused)

op 17: clear flags

op 23: if $BEBD below (unused)

Message start, short first line: starts canned message X like $8DAA, but first counts one frame in $E0, so that the message's first line is 24 characters instead of 25. Its only caller, $98BA, prints an object's name when an object with bit 3 of $29C0 is taken or boarded: for those objects message n is object n's name, 24 characters wide. Does nothing while a message is printing.

Message start: starts canned message X (0-63). While a message is printing ($E6 non-zero) the request is dropped. Otherwise it points the token read ($8E27/$8E28) at the message through the split table $20A0 (low) / $20E0 (high), whose entries point one byte before the first token, zeroes the token and character indexes $DE and $DF and sets $E6 = $FF. Callers: ops 20 and 27, LOCKED ($9432), TOO HEAVY ($984A), an object's name ($8DA4), a room's name or the dark-room warning ($AEE8), and $878B, $8979, $B3DA, $B43B.

Message tick: Benson's message window, once a frame from the panel interrupt ($BA51) while $E6 is non-zero. $E0 counts frames: on counts 1-25 it scrolls the window $5F78-$5F8E (screen row 22, columns 8-30) one cell to the left, puts the character $FC in the right-hand cell, sounds SID voice 3 at frequency (character AND $3F) + $30 (high byte; 0 for a blank) and fetches the next character; from 26 it silences voice 3 and waits until $E0 reaches $E1, the pause length (the scripts poke it; $7D in play, 99 frames), then restarts the count and lowers $E6. Text therefore scrolls in lines of 25 characters, one a frame, with a pause after each line. While $E6 is negative the characters come from the message ($8E05); after the end token $E6 is 1, the line is padded with blanks and the printer stops at the next pause ($E6 = 0).

Character read: LDA (text) + DF, the next character of the current word, literal or figure. Its operand $8E0A/$8E0B is rewritten to point one byte before the text ($8E40/$8E46 for a dictionary word, $8E58/$8E61 for a literal, $8E7E/$8E85 for a figure), so DF = 1 reads the first character; in the snapshot it points at itself. The character c becomes the glyph (c AND $7F), plus $80 when that is 10 or more, in $FC: letters, stored as ASCII, land on the window font (ASCII + $80), values 0-9 on the figures $00-$09 and $0A-$0F on * + , - . / ($8A-$8F). Bit 7 of c ends the word (DF back to 0).
pointer patched: text - 1
Low byte of the character read's pointer at $8E09, written by $8E40 (dictionary word), $8E58 (literal) and $8E7E (figure).
High byte of the character read's pointer, written by $8E46, $8E61 and $8E85; the code that follows turns the character into a glyph and moves DF on.

Next token (when DF is 0): puts a blank in $FC, advances the token index $DE and reads token $DE through the LDY at $8E26. 0 ends the message ($8E50 sets $E6 = 1); $01-$EE is a dictionary word, whose pointer from $2120 (low) / $2210 (high) goes into $8E0A/$8E0B (words 1-7, endings, follow straight on; later words show this blank first); $EF is the blank alone; $F0-$F7 take the word number from $57D8-$57DF ($56E8 + token; no message in this image uses them); $F8-$FE are figures ($8E74); $FF starts literal text ($8E55).

Token read: LDY (message) + DE. Its operand $8E27/$8E28 points one byte before the message's first token: at the op 1 byte itself ($8C38/$8C3D) or through a canned message's pointer ($8DB1/$8DB7); in the snapshot it points at itself.
pointer patched: message - 1
Low byte of the token read's pointer at $8E26, written by $8C38 (op 1) and $8DB7 (canned message); $8E55 copies it for a literal.
High byte of the token read's pointer, written by $8C3D (op 1) and $8DB1 (canned message).

Literal text (token $FF): points the character read ($8E0A/$8E0B) and the scan at $8E6C ($8E6D/$8E6E) at the message itself, sets DF to the literal's first character (the byte after the $FF) and moves DE to its last character, the one with bit 7 set, so that the next token follows it. The blank already in $FC is shown first. DE and DF are single bytes, so a message cannot run past 255 bytes.
Literal scan: LDA (message) + X, stepping X on until a character with bit 7 set, the literal's end. Its operand $8E6D/$8E6E is written by $8E5B/$8E64; in the snapshot it points at itself.
pointer patched: message - 1
Low byte of the literal scan's pointer, a copy of $8E27 written by $8E5B.
High byte of the literal scan's pointer, a copy of $8E28 written by $8E64.

Figure (tokens $F8-$FE): formats counter 8 + k (k = token AND 7), the four BCD bytes at $7700 + 4k, as decimal digits at $7720 + 8k with no leading zeros (a single 0 when it is zero) and bit 7 on the last digit, and points the character read at $771F + 8k with DF = 1. Counter 8 is the credits and 9 the reward on offer (tokens $F8, $F9); counter 15 cannot be printed, $FF being the literal token.

Build road list: picks the roads to draw outdoors for a view radius A in grid squares (from the altitude table $2A00, called by $955D when the radius or the player's square changes). The window is the box of 2A + 1 squares a side round the player's square ($74, $7A), clipped to the city by $8F7F on each axis. It first loads the four map bytes of the player's own location $B7 into vertex slots $3C-$3F ($757C-$757F: the ends of the roads along its row and its column, which edges 1 and 2 join; all 0 outside the city), then, square by square over the window, patches the map readers at $8F66-$8F79 with each row's first location and adds the road along the square's row ($2C00 to $2D00) and along its column ($2E00 to $2F00) through $8FC3. The vertex list ($7540, slots $B5 up to $3F) and the edge list ($7580/$75C0, edges 3 up to $B6) start empty. $EE = 0 marks the whole city built, so that asking again returns at once. With radius 0 only the player's own square's roads are listed.
low byte patched: row start

Map reader, low byte of LDX $2C00,Y at $8F66: the first location of the window row being scanned (written by $8EF1, 16 added a row by $8F58). $2C00 + location: where the road along that square's row begins, as a location number (its lowest X), 0 when the square has none.
low byte patched: row start
Map reader, low byte of LDA $2D00,Y at $8F6B, kept equal to $8F67. $2D00 + location: where the road along that square's row ends (its highest X).
low byte patched: row start
Map reader, low byte of LDX $2E00,Y at $8F71, kept equal to $8F67. $2E00 + location: where the road along that square's column begins (its lowest Y), 0 when the square has none.
low byte patched: row start

Map reader, low byte of LDA $2F00,Y at $8F76, kept equal to $8F67. $2F00 + location: where the road along that square's column ends (its highest Y). Every square a road crosses lists the whole road, ends included.

Road window, one axis: A = the player's square on that axis ($74 or $7A), $08 = the radius r, $09 = 2r + 1. Returns the window's first square in A and its width in X, clipped to the city's squares 0-15, with the carry clear; the carry set means the window misses the city on this axis. The first square is taken as signed, so a player out in the wasteland on either side is clipped correctly.

Road vertex slot: looks for location A in the vertex list $7540 + X, X from $B5 to $3F, and returns its slot in A; if absent, it lowers $B5 and stores A in the new slot. Nothing checks the list against its 64 slots, but the map's 32 roads have only 52 distinct ends and 60 slots ($00-$3B) are free below the four fixed ones.

Road add: adds the road from location X to location A (the two ends of a row or column road) to the edge list, unless either end is the player's own location $B7 (such a road runs through the player's square, whose roads are edges 1 and 2 already) or the same pair of slots is listed. Slots come from $8FAE; a new edge goes in at $B6 + 1 with $7580 the slot of A and $75C0 the slot of X, the order of edges 1 and 2, so the duplicate test also catches the player's own roads.

Road list preset: loads a prepared road list from $902A + Y: the first vertex slot (into $B5), the vertex locations up to slot $3F, the last edge number (into $B6), then edges 3 onwards as slot pairs. Also sets $B9 and $EE to $40 so that the next radius-based build ($8EC2) starts afresh. Only Y = 0 is used, from $953C: at height $200000 and above ($77 >= $20) the road list is the overview at $902A.

Road overview, the road list drawn high up ($8FF8 at height $200000 and above): first slot $2E; 18 locations for slots $2E-$3F: $01 $0F $FF $F1 (the ring 01-00, 15-00, 15-15, 01-15 round the city), $33 $3C $7C $73 (the ring 03-03, 12-03, 12-07, 03-07), $04 $34, $0A $FA, $51 $5F, and for slots $3C-$3F $75 $F5, $D1 $DC; last edge $0D; edges 3-13 as slot pairs ($2E-$2F ... $3A-$3B). With edges 1 and 2 that is 13 main roads, a simplified city map (the map itself has 32 roads).

Draw roads, once a pass outdoors (main loop $85B0): sets the line routines' pattern ($AE02) and, unless $EF is non-zero, puts every listed road end on the ground: the height -($77:$76) goes through $9E93 into $54/$55 for all of them, each vertex slot from $B5 to $3F holding a location is placed at the centre of that square relative to the player ($A67B) and projected ($A75C), and edges 3 to $B6 are drawn ($99DD). Edges 1 and 2, the roads through the player's own square, are drawn only when off the ground ($77 non-zero) and $CA is 0; otherwise the main loop draws the square's local model instead ($85B3-$85C2).

Go through door: takes the player into room $08, arriving at the door whose X byte is at offset $09 of that room's descriptor (from the main loop at $857E once $9437 has found a door, and from $A2E0 at the foot of an elevator: room $CD, its first door). Room 0 is the outside: $A8 (underground) and $CD (current room) become 0, the object list and sight are redone ($9374), $A9 = 9 (the craft the player is in; $9D99 loads its parameters), $B232 resets the colours $C2-$C5 ($C4, the background, to green) and the sight's light grey, the position becomes the nine bytes at $90ED, $AF6E runs with $C8 = 0 (then $C8 = $7F) and $950D recomputes the location. Any other room goes to $90F6.

Room exit position: where a door into room 0 puts the player, nine bytes copied to $72-$7A by $90D5: X $0867C0, height $40F880, Y $087000 (over square 08-08). Only room $AB has such a door. Object 63 is at X $087000, height $40FCC0, Y $087000, just beside and above this point; by its height probably the Colony Craft, which the leaflet puts high above the city.

Enter room X (not 0): points $1B/$1C at its descriptor through the split table $2300 (low) / $23C0 (high) and sets $8D = $E0. A transporter room (bit 7 of byte 0: rooms $72-$87) first rewrites its own door, byte 5 (arrival bits 4-6) and byte 6 (destination), from the pair at bytes 10-11, or at 12-13 when the player came from the room named in byte 10; room $72 takes one of the eight pairs at bytes 10-25 at random. It then sets $F0 = 10 (the transporter sound plays and doors stay shut meanwhile, $AED6, $9437), and room $7F also mirrors the world ($9353). The player is placed at the arrival door, X from its byte 2 and Y from its byte 3 into $73 and $79, low bytes $80 along the wall and 0 across it by the door's bit 7; $CD = X and the room is built ($9162).

Build room: makes the current room's model from its descriptor ($1B/$1C) in the local model tables: vertex X $0400 (low) / $0440 (high), height $0480 / $04C0, Y $0500 / $0540, edges $0580 (from) / $05C0 (to). First redoes the object list and sight ($9374), sets $74 = $7A = 0, clears $F7 and the tables. The room is a box of eight vertices and 12 edges ($933B/$9347): X size byte 0 AND $7F, Y size byte 2 AND $7F, height byte 1 AND 7 (high bytes); byte 3 goes to $C4, the view's background colour, and byte 4 to $C5, and the sight sprite turns white ($91DF). Each door entry, 4 bytes from byte 5 (flags, destination, X, Y; a 0 ends the list), adds its outline ($922F). A list ended by $80 is a dark room: unless the Photon Emitter (object 16) is carried or in the room, $C2 = $C4 = $C5 = 0 and $F7 = 1 (message 1, ITS VERY DARK IN HERE). Then byte 1's top five bits name the room: with bit 7 of byte 2 a script started at once ($8A8C), otherwise a message left in $F7 for $AEE4; $98 = $FF, $939E keeps the player inside and voice 1 is silenced.

Room add door: X = 4 for a door with bit 7 clear (in a wall of constant Y) or 5 with bit 7 set (constant X), written into the STA at $9256 by $9235. The door type (bits 0-3) picks an outline from $928A through the offsets at $932B; each outline point (offset along the wall, height, both low bytes) becomes a vertex in the door's square (entry bytes 2 and 3 into $0440 and $0540), and the new vertices are joined in order by edges ($926E). $70 and $71 hold the last vertex and edge numbers so far.
page patched by $9235: $04 or $05

Page of the store STA $0400,Y at $9256: written by $9235 with 4 (a point's along-wall offset goes to X low, $0400) or 5 (to Y low, $0500). The rest of the loop stores each point's height in $0480 and the door's square in $0440/$0540, and $926E joins the new vertices into a line of edges in $0580/$05C0.

Door outlines, 13 of them to $932A, each a list of points (offset along the wall, height) ended by $FF, joined in order by $922F; offsets are within the door's grid square (so $50-$B0 is its middle), heights in the low byte of the room's height. This one, for door types 0, 1, 2 and 8 (only 2 is used, by 293 doors): a plain frame open at the bottom, $50,$00 $50,$C0 $B0,$C0 $B0,$00.
Door type 3 outline (9 doors): the plain frame, then up the right post to a triangle across its upper half, $B0,$60 $80,$A0 $50,$60 $B0,$60.
Door type 4 outline (2 doors): the plain frame and an upward arrow up its middle, shaft $80,$00 to $80,$A0, head back to $70,$80 and $90,$80.
