Door type 5 outline (2 doors): the plain frame and a downward arrow, head at $80,$00 through $70,$20 and $90,$20, shaft up to $80,$A0.
Door type 6 outline (38 doors, the transporter rooms among them): a frame with both diagonals, a cross.
Door type 7 outline (30 doors, transporter rooms too): the plain frame and one diagonal, $B0,$00 to $50,$C0.

Door type 9 outline (13 doors): a triangle, $30,$00 $80,$C0 $D0,$00. Types 8-15 are locked ($9493) unless object 8 + type is carried, or object 48 ($948E): this one needs object 17, and types 10-15 need objects 18-23, the keys.
Door type 10 outline (8 doors, key object 18): a trapezium narrowing upwards, $40,$00 $60,$C0 $A0,$C0 $C0,$00.
Door type 11 outline (6 doors, key object 19): a pentagon, $48,$00 $25,$6B $80,$AC $DB,$6B $B8,$00.
Door type 12 outline (6 doors, key object 20): straight sides and a pointed top, $50,$00 $50,$A0 $80,$C0 $B0,$A0 $B0,$00.
Door type 13 outline (6 doors, key object 21): a trapezium widening upwards, $60,$00 $40,$C0 $C0,$C0 $A0,$00.
Door type 14 outline (6 doors, key object 22): a hexagon, $60,$00 $40,$60 $60,$C0 $A0,$C0 $C0,$60 $A0,$00.
Door type 15 outline (8 doors, key object 23): straight sides and a bevelled top, $50,$00 $50,$80 $70,$C0 $90,$C0 $B0,$80 $B0,$00.
Door outline offsets: for door types 0-15, the offset of the type's outline from $928A, read at $923B: $00 $00 $00 $09 $1A $2D $40 $4D $00 $58 $5F $68 $73 $7E $87 $94.

Room box, the first vertex of each of its 12 edges, read as $933A + Y for Y = 1-12 ($933B-$9346, copied to edges 0-11 at $0580-$058B by $918F): 0 1 2 3 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7. The byte at $933A itself is the last door-outline offset (type 15).

Room box, the second vertex of each edge, $9346 + Y for Y = 1-12 ($9347-$9352, to $05C0-$05CB): 1 2 3 0 4 5 6 7 5 6 7 4. Vertices 0-3 (at the room's height) and 4-7 (at 0) make two rectangles joined by four uprights. The byte at $9346 itself is the previous list's last entry.

Mirror world, for transporter room $7F on entry ($9145): flips $F1, which swaps the joystick's left and right ($A165) and is EORed in at $A360, $A376, $A3D7, $AA13, $AFE1, $AFFD, $B057 and $B08B (the reversing transporter), and flips bit 6 of $29C0 for objects 1 to $EB (the number carried): it loads each carried object's number into Y but indexes with X, so it flips the wrong objects' bit, which nothing reads. Sets $F0 = $1F, a longer transporter effect, and returns X = $7F for the caller.

List room objects: shows the gun sight, sprite 0, only while object 40 (the Sights) is carried (bit 7 of $29E8 into $D015), and lists at $2981 onwards every object whose room in $2940 is the current room $CD (0 outdoors), from object $B4 ($3F) down; $B2 = how many. Also sets $C2 = 1. Twelve callers, among them taking an object ($9843), the room exit ($90C6) and the room build ($9162).

Keep in room: holds the player inside the room, $20 from each wall: X ($73:$72) between 0.$20 and (X size $0440 - 1).$DF, Y ($79:$78) likewise with the Y size $0540; a stop at the 0 side also zeroes $74 or $7A. Returns in A and $F8 the walls touched as a negative count (0: none); the first pass against a wall starts voice 1 sound $14 ($B958). The main loop then looks for a door there ($8570, $9437).

Is object A carried? Searches the carried stack $BEB1-$BEBA (depth $EB) from the most recent down. Out: Z set and X = its slot (0-9) when found; X = $FF with N set when not. Used by script op 12 ($8B3A) and by the dark-room test at $91F4 (object $10, the PHOTON EMITTER).

Is object A in the player's location? Searches the location list $2981 to $2980+$B2 (objects whose $2940 equals $CD, built at $9380). Out: Z set and X = its index when found; X = $FF with N set when not. Used at $91F9: a dark room is lit when the PHOTON EMITTER lies in it.
door_check's refusal (reached only from $949F): prints canned message 0, LOCKED, and returns carry clear, so the door stays shut.

Underground: may the player pass the wall just touched? Called from the complex loop ($8579) when $939E reports a wall and $B1 is 0; nothing while $F0 is non-zero. Walks the room's door list from ($1B)+5, four bytes a door: flags (bit 7: door in a wall crossed along X; bits 6-4: arrival door in the next room; bits 3-0: type), destination room (0 = the surface), X cell, Y cell; flags 0 or $80 end it. A door matches when the player's mid bytes equal its cell (rounded across the wall, truncated along it), the low byte along the wall is mid-cell ($40-$BF for Y, $28-$A7 for X) and across it near the edge, and the heading ($2C/$2D) rounded to a quarter turn lies along the crossing axis. Types 8-15 need object $10+(type-8) carried unless object $30 is, else door_locked. Open: C set, $08 = destination, $09 = 4 x arrival door + 7 (its offset in that room's data), $C8 = $7F or $FF (from heading and side), SID voice 1 control cleared. Otherwise C clear.
Eight single-bit masks, $01 to $80 (bit n at $94D8+n). Nothing indexes the table; its one reader is BIT $94DD at $87CD.
The bit-5 mask ($20) of bit_masks, used as an operand: BIT $94DD at $87CD tests bit 5 of location $F5's $2B00 byte.

City loop, once a pass ($85A4), skipped while an elevator moves ($CA): ($8C,$8D) = a float of the height for the view-centre offset $A320 applies ($76/16 while $77 = 0, else 16). If the grid square $74/$7A is still the one remembered in $85/$87 only set_view_range runs; otherwise enter_square.

Sets up the grid square the player stands in. $B9 = $FF (so the view range is rebuilt), $B7 = the map index Y x 16 + X (0 outside the 16 x 16 city, which also leaves 00-00 without a building); a non-zero index loads that location's building (load_building). Falls into set_view_range. Called at start-up ($7287), restart ($80DF), on leaving a complex ($90EA), from $A2B0, and from city_view_update when the square changes.

Picks the view range from the height. From height $20:00:00 up: the fixed line set at $902A ($8FF8 with Y = 0). Below: $B9 = $2A00[min(height >> 11, 255)], 0 to 63 grid squares (also the far-object range in draw_object), and $8EC2 rebuilds the city-grid lines when it changes. Then $70/$71 = the building's last vertex and edge numbers, and $85/$86/$87 = square X, height high byte, square Y remembered.

Loads the building of location A (map index) into the vertex and edge tables. Pointer from $2600 (low) / $2700 (high) + A; $F2 = $2B00+A (bit 7: destroyed). Model: last vertex number ($88/$89), last edge number ($8A/$8B), the edge number from which edges take the second line form ($98, $FF none), a rotating-part byte (0 none; else low nibble + 1 rotating vertices $9F, high nibble x 8 the spin step $A2, then centre X and Y mid bytes $A0/$A1). Edges into $0580 (from) and $05C0 (to): one byte of two 4-bit vertex numbers each until a 0 byte, then two bytes each (numbers up to $3F, which reach the city-grid points $9054 keeps in the top slots). Vertices: the rotating ones first, 3 bytes (X radius, height mid, Y radius; radii x 64 as floats into $57A0/$57B0 and $57C0/$57D0), then fixed ones of 2 or 3 bytes (building_coord); every vertex takes the player's square as its high bytes ($0740, $07C0). A destroyed building is flattened at once (collapse_building).

Reads the next model byte for load_building: its top two bits are shifted into $06, building a 4-bit height code over a vertex's X and Y bytes; its low six bits c give the mid byte: 0 = $00 and $3F = $FF (the square's edges), else c + $60 ($61-$9E, around the centre $80). Height code 0-14 is the height mid byte; 15 reads one more byte: below $80 the height mid itself, else bits 6-4 mid and bits 3-0 x 16 low.
Flattens a destroyed building at once: repeats collapse_step until nothing moves. Called by load_building when the location's $2B00 bit 7 is set.

One step of a building falling down: each vertex 0 to $89 whose height mid byte ($04C0) is above 0 drops by one and moves one unit toward the square's centre $80 in X ($0440) and Y ($0540). Out: A = minus the number moved (Z set once flat). Called by the destruction sequence $879B: each pass at $87B4 while the countdown $F4 runs at the hit location $F5, and $F4 times at $882B after the ANTI TIME BOMB path ($8816) reloads the building; and by collapse_building.

Transforms and projects the current building's vertices $70 down to 0: $A5CE turns each one (X $0400/$0440/$0740, height $0480/$04C0/$0780, Y $0500/$0540/$07C0) into player-relative floats, $A75C applies the view matrix and perspective and fills that vertex slot.

Draws the current building's edges $71 down to 0 with draw_edge, vertex pairs from $0580/$05C0. Starts with the OR line form set by $AE02 and switches to the AND form ($ADFC) at edge number $98, the model's second line colour.

Objects, once a pass (city $85D8, complex $8595): the new key $E9 goes to $B8, and T ($16) or B ($1C) is consumed ($B4B2) so it acts once. Then draw_object for each object in the location list, from $2980+$B2 down to $2981.

Takes, boards or draws object X (kept in $AF). Model pointer $2800/$2840 into $1D/$1E; offset from the player (object_offset); T or B (take_or_board; if it acted, nothing is drawn). Within one grid square on every axis the model is drawn: offsets less $800 each, vertices read and transformed ($A61F) and projected ($A75C) into slots 0 to n ($97B5), edges drawn ($97CD pairs, $97E1 nibbles). Farther, a single dot ($ADCB) if the object is at or above the player's height, or below it within $B9 squares; else nothing. Model: last vertex number; 3 signed bytes a vertex (X, height, Y, units of 16; objects 0-15 turned by $800A/$801A/$802A); an edge byte n: below $80, n+1 edges of one byte (two 4-bit vertex numbers), else (n AND $7F)+1 edges of two bytes.
far object: one projected point, drawn as a dot
near object: offsets less $800 on each axis, paired with the EOR #$80 of the vertex bytes at $A6F1
vertex loop: read, transform ($A61F), project into slot $19 ($A75C)
edges stored as byte pairs
edges stored as two 4-bit vertex numbers per byte

T and B for object $AF (key in $B8). T: within 256 units on every axis; refused (C set) if its $29C0 bit 4 is set (fixed; the KITCHEN SINK, object $2F, overrides), or bit 5 (heavy: canned message 2, TOO HEAVY; the ANTIGRAV, object $1B, overrides), or 10 objects are already carried. Taken: pushed on the carried stack ($EB+1, into $BEB0+$EB), $29C0 bit 7 set, $2940 = $FF, object_event, list rebuilt ($9374), C clear. B: on foot only ($A9 bit 7), objects 0-7, within 512 units: the player takes its X and Y, the heading from $802A, $A9 = its number, its motion record (load_motion_record), the view matrix ($A320), speed zeroed, the craft taken out of the world ($2940 = $FF); C clear.

What taking or boarding object X triggers, from its $29C0 flags in A: bit 3 prints its name (canned message X, when the window is free, $8DA4), bit 2 starts script X as a call ($8A8C); either, both or neither. Then sound 0 ($B94D) with X = $AF.

L, and the end of a hard landing ($A0DA): leave the craft $A9. Nothing on foot ($A9 bit 7) or airborne ($7F = 0). Roll $28/$29 cleared, pitch $2A/$2B = $200 (level), speed stopped (stop_craft), $A9 = $80. Craft 0-7: heading >> 4 kept in $802A+n, then placed at the player (place_object). Mode 9, falling: nothing placed. Mode 10, the intro's descent: object 10 is placed, the intro's crashed ship left at the crash site.

D: drops the object taken last. Only when landed ($7F non-zero) unless object $38, the pyramid, is carried (then dropped objects stay at the player's height); nothing when none is carried ($EB = 0). Pops it from $BEB0+$EB, clears its $29C0 bit 7, sound 0, then place_object.

Puts object Y in the current location ($2940 = $CD) at the player's X and Y (all three bytes) and height (mid and high from $76/$77, low 0), then rebuilds the location list ($9374). Shared by drop_object and leave_craft.
Sets the exponent bytes of the throttle ($ED) and speed ($27) floats to $88, which is effectively zero. Called at start-up, restart, boarding, leaving, and by the E key ($B47B).

Object X's position minus the player's, three 24-bit differences (low, mid, high): X ($2880/$2480/$2540 less $72-$74) into $D5-$D7, height ($28C0/$24C0/$2580 less $75-$77) into $D8-$DA, Y ($2900/$2500/$25C0 less $78-$7A) into $DB-$DD.

Is the offset in $D5-$DD inside a cube? X (low) and Y (high) give a limit in units of 256; each axis's absolute value, shifted right 8 bits, is compared with it (abs_compare). Out: C clear when all three are below it, C set at the first that is not. Limits used: 1 for T, 2 for B, $100 (one grid square) and $B9 x $100 in draw_object.
Makes the signed 24-bit value A (low), X (mid), Y (high) positive and compares its mid and high bytes with $08/$09. Out: C set when it is at least that limit.

Draws the edge between vertex slots X and Y, clipped to the 160 x 136 view. Per slot the projector ($A75C) left: clip flags $0700 (bit 7 behind the eye, bit 0 X off screen, bit 1 Y off screen), screen X and Y $0680/$06C0, projected X and Y as floats $0600/$03C0 and $7600/$0640, view-space X, Y, depth floats $0100/$0140, $0180/$02C0, $0340/$0380. Both ends behind: nothing. The start is an end on screen if there is one, else the end in front, else (both off screen) the farther. Both in front: the direction is the difference of the projected positions; end behind: edge_end_behind. Slope $68/$69 = dY/dX, $66 = minor/major x 256, $67 = signs and steepness; then edge_octant, edge_clip_start, edge_plot.
both ends in front: dX, dY from the projected positions

draw_edge when the end vertex is behind the eye: the screen direction is taken from view space as (x2 - x1 x d2/d1, y2 - y1 x d2/d1), the way the projected line heads as the edge nears the eye's plane; signs to $67 and slope to $68/$69 as for a visible end.

Picks the line routine: $67 (bit 0 dY negative, bit 1 dX negative, bit 2 steep) indexes $BBD0 for the octant 0-7, whose routine address ($BC38/$BC40) goes to $04/$05. If the end is not on screen, the end point becomes the screen corner the line heads for ($BBD8/$BBE0: X 0 or 159, Y 0 or 135), so the routine runs to the edge. A start on screen goes straight to edge_plot.
octant routine address into $04/$05

The start is off screen but in front: its region (clip flags and the signs of its projected X and Y through $BBE8) with the direction ($67 >> 1) indexes $BBF8 for the screen edges the line can enter by (bit 0 right X=159, 1 bottom Y=135, 2 left X=0, 3 top Y=0), 0 = reject; an end in front is tested the same way against $BC18. Each allowed edge is tried in turn: the crossing is found from the start's projected position and the slope against the edge values $90-$97 (left, right, top, bottom; $21 the scale exponent) and kept if it falls inside the other axis's range; it becomes the start. No crossing: nothing is drawn.

Hands the line to the octant routine: X = start column $6A, Y = start row $6B, $08 = $80 (the fraction accumulator at one half), JMP ($0004). The routine draws toward $6C/$6D, stepping the minor axis by $66/256.
JMP ($0004): into the octant routine

Copies motion record A (16 bytes at $9DAD + 16 x A) into $BEA0-$BEAF. A is the motion mode $A9: 0-7 the craft (objects 0-7), 9 falling, 10 the intro's descent. $BEA0/$BEA1 is the motion routine that JMP ($BEA0) at $A178 runs each pass while $A8 = 0 and $A9 is below $80.
writes all of $BEA0-$BEAF, the motion routine pointer $BEA0/$BEA1 included

Motion records, 16 bytes each, indexed by $A9 (load_motion_record). Flight layout: +0 motion routine, +2 float turn damping, +4 float turn step, +6 pitch step, +7 bank (roll = turn rate x 2^(n/4); $80 up none), +8 float climb factor, +10 float speed damping, +12 read by no code found ($10 in records 0-7), +13 ceiling (height high byte; above it the climb halves per unit), +14 float thrust. Record 0, craft 0: motion_flight, turn damping 0.94, turn step 1, pitch step 8, climb 0.5, speed damping 0.5, ceiling $5A, thrust 0.91.

Record 1, craft 1 (the DOMINION DART, for sale at 08-08): motion_flight like record 0 but ceiling $0A and thrust 0.39; carrying the POWERAMP (object $1C) in it raises the ceiling to $5A and doubles the throttle ($9F8A, $A050).
Record 2, craft 2: motion_ground, a ground vehicle; turn damping near 0 (no turn memory), turn step 16, pitch step 0, climb 0.25, speed damping 0.5, ceiling $01, thrust 0.20.
Record 3, craft 3: motion_flight; turn damping 0.89, turn step 2, pitch step 12, climb 1.0, speed damping 0.75, ceiling $5A, thrust 0.20.
Record 4, craft 4: motion_flight without banking (+7 = $88); turn step 2, pitch step 8, climb 1.0, speed damping 0.25, ceiling $01, thrust 0.39.
Record 5, craft 5: motion_ground, a ground vehicle; turn damping 0.94, turn step 1, speed damping 0.5, ceiling $01, thrust 0.91.
Record 6, craft 6: motion_flight like record 0 (ceiling $5A) with thrust 0.78.
Record 7, craft 7 (the interstellar ship; script 7 tests $A9 = 7): motion_starship, which reads none of the flight values here.

Record 8, never loaded whole: at a landing with the pitch at $200-$3FF, $A0CC levels the pitch and copies its bytes 2-11 over the craft's (turn damping near 0, turn step 16, pitch step 1, climb 1.0, speed damping 0.25), keeping the routine: the handling on the ground. Take-off reloads the craft's own record ($A0FF).
Record 8 bytes 2-11, the ground handling: $A0CC-$A0D5 (LDA $9E2F,X) copies these ten bytes to $BEA2-$BEAB when a craft lands, leaving its motion routine in place.
Record 9, falling (set at $898A, $90CD, $A1E3): motion_fall; +2 = $2F taken from the height mid byte each pass, +3/+4/+5 = $10/$15/$0D added to roll, pitch and heading, so the view tumbles.
Record 10, the intro's descent (set at start-up, $7246): motion_descent_1; +2 = $20, the fall per pass of its last stage (motion_fall), +3 = $08 added to the roll each pass.

Motion routine of record 7: JMP $AA62, which holds the pitch at $1xx until $BEFE is set (script 7 pokes it at $1123 when the launch goes ahead, after PRESS Y TO LAUNCH and the advert check), then flies the starfield.

Second stage of the intro's descent (pointer set at $9E8D): with the height high byte $77 at 0 it goes on as motion_fall (record 10's $20 a pass); else the height $77:$76 drops by the descent step for $77 >> 1, then motion_spin.

First stage of the intro's descent, from height $7F:00 (start-up): the height $77:$76 drops by the descent step for $77 >> 3 each pass while height_to_float shows heights x 8. When $77 reaches 0 it patches height_to_float to a plain JMP $8510, sets $77 = 6 (about where the x 8 view had got to) and points the motion routine at motion_descent_2. Each pass ends in motion_spin.
self-modifying: JSR $8510 at $9E93 becomes JMP $8510
motion pointer becomes $9E60 (high byte $9E left by record 10)

Height offset to float for the far views (city-grid points $9068, object dots $976C): $8510, then 12 added to the exponent byte (x 8) during the intro's first descent stage; $9E84 rewrites the JSR as JMP $8510 when that stage ends, and nothing restores it.

Intro descent steps, split word table (low bytes here, high at descent_step_hi): taken from the height $77:$76 each pass by motion_descent_1 (index $77 >> 3) and motion_descent_2 (index $77 >> 1): $0040, $0080, then $80 more a step to $0700, and $0800 at 15.
High bytes of the intro descent steps (descent_step_lo holds the low bytes and the values).
Falling (record 9) and the intro's last stage: the height mid byte loses $BEA2 each pass; below 0 goes to crash_landing, else motion_spin.

Touch-down as a crash: $FA = 0, carry set, to $A0AF (height 0, on the ground; with carry set it calls leave_craft and sets $F9 = 2). From motion_fall and from motion_ground when a ground craft comes down.

Adds $BEA3, $BEA4, $BEA5 to roll $28/$29, pitch $2A/$2B and heading $2C/$2D (16-bit adds, not masked), then $A12B, which turns the building's rotating parts. Tail of motion_fall and both descent stages.

Ground craft (records 2, 5): pitch step forced to 0, eye height low byte $75 = $3F, then motion_flight. Off the ground ($7F = 0) the height high byte drops by one a pass; below 0 goes to crash_landing, which throws the player out.

Flight model of the aircraft (records 0, 1, 3, 4, 6; record 8's values on the ground), each pass through JMP ($BEA0); an elevator ride ($CA) goes to $A24A instead. Turn rate $22/$23 (float) x turn damping $BEA2/3, plus or minus the turn step $BEA4/5 while the stick ($80) is pushed left or right; the pitch $2A/$2B (10 bits) moves by $BEA6 with the stick up or down. Speed $26/$27 = (speed + throttle $EC/$ED x thrust $BEAE/F) x speed damping $BEAA/B; the throttle counts double in craft 1 with the POWERAMP carried. Y ($78-$7A) and X ($72-$74) then move by speed x cos pitch x cos or sin heading ($38/$39, $3E/$3F, $3C/$3D from $A544). Continues past $A000 to $A13C: take-off speed, climb (lift $BEA8/9, ceiling $BEAD), landing and crash, bank.
throttle x thrust + speed, x speed damping
Y += speed x cos pitch x cos heading
X += speed x cos pitch x sin heading

Vehicle model, part 2 (it starts at $9F17, entered by JMP ($BEA0) at $A178): X ($74:$73:$72) += the whole part (floor, $84A7 at $9FFE) of v*cos(pitch)*sin(heading), sign-extended; v is the speed float $26/$27. Level pitch is 512, where cos = -1, so a positive v moves north at heading 0 and west at 256. Ground hold: when the grounded flag $7F is set, unless the craft is on the Colony Craft deck ($FA) and off its pad ($A13D carry set), a speed under 128 units a pass (exponent byte of $27 under $1C, either sign) sets the pitch level ($2B:$2A = $200) and skips the height step (JMP $A102); 128 or more lets the craft pitch and climb, which is take-off.
grounded?
on the deck: off the pad starts a fall
|v| >= 128: free to pitch and climb
under take-off speed: level, no height step

Vehicle model, part 3, height step: height ($77:$76:$75) += floor(v*sin(pitch)*k), sign-extended, k being the float with mantissa $BEA8 and exponent byte $BEA9. Climbing above the ceiling ($77 over $BEAD; $5A instead in vehicle 1 while object 28, the POWERAMP, is carried: $29DC bit 7), k becomes (1+$BEA8/256)*2^($BEAD-$77): it halves for each 65536 above, and from 32 above it is nil (2^-30 or less). Descending is never damped. Then: negative or under 64 goes to the touchdown test $A09A, a non-zero high byte to the Colony Craft check $A0E2 (which wants $40), anything else is airborne ($A0F7).
descending: never damped
the ceiling, a height high byte
POWERAMP carried in vehicle 1: ceiling $5A
far above the ceiling: no climb

Vehicle model, part 4: the craft reached the ground (height under 64, or negative). Crash (carry set into $A0AF) if this pass's height step was 256 or more (the exponent byte in $09, left by the multiply at $A06E, 8 or more), or if the pitch taken as $2B:$2A >> 2 is 160 or more: pitch 640-1023, nose down more than 45 degrees or past the vertical. Pitch 0-639, including nose up and upside down, lands safely. Horizontal speed is not tested.
height step >= 256 a pass: crash
pitch >= 640: crash

Vehicle model, part 5, the landing itself; carry set means a crash. Also entered by JMP from $9ED3 with carry set, at the end of a fall ($9EBE: the tumble from the Colony Craft, a ground vehicle off its deck via $9F13, and the opening descent). Height = 63 ($00:$00:$3F), roll $29:$28 = 0, grounded flag $7F = $3F. A pitch of 512-1023 is levelled to 512 and the ground handling loaded: the 10 bytes at $9E2F (vehicle record 8, bytes 2-11) into $BEA2-$BEAB: turning 16 a pass with no inertia, pitch 1 a pass, speed kept x0.25 a pass. Safe: on to $A102. Crash: JSR $98C8 (leave the vehicle, as the L key does), $F9 = 2 (on the second pass after, $AFCA calls the crash effect $B242), RTS.
pitch under 512 (nose up): left as it is
crash: out of the vehicle

Vehicle model, part 6: height high byte positive and non-zero. At exactly $40 and over the Colony Craft pad ($A13D: square 08-08, X and Y middle bytes $68-$77, height middle byte $FC or more) the craft lands on the deck: $76 = $FF, deck flag $FA = $FF, then the landing at $A0B6 with no crash test (height $40:$FF:$3F, carry clear). Otherwise airborne ($A0F7). The deck is solid only for heights $40FC00-$40FFFF, so a craft climbing into that band over the pad is also put on it.
only at height $40xxxx

Vehicle model, part 7, airborne: grounded flag $7F = 0, deck flag $FA = 0, and the vehicle's own 16-byte record reloaded into $BEA0-$BEAF (JSR $9D99 with A = vehicle number $A9), which undoes the ground handling a landing loads. Runs on every airborne pass.

Vehicle model, part 8, turn and bank: heading $2D:$2C += the whole part of the turn rate $22/$23, a float the stick steers at $9F1E-$9F58 (the sign, added as carry, turns $84A7's ones' complement into two's complement; $2D is not masked here, its readers use the low 2 bits). Airborne only ($7F = 0): roll $29:$28 = whole part of turn rate * 2^($BEA7/4), x4 for the flying craft ($BEA7 = 8); a negative $BEA7 (vehicle 4) gives no bank. Falls into $A12B.
sign to carry: two's complement
bank scale; negative: no bank

Last step of every movement model (JMP from $9EFA and $A1EA, fall-through from $A129): unless bit 7 of $F2 is set (the current location's flags, $2B00 + location, loaded at $9583), the spin angle $9A:$99 += $A2, the spin rate from the location's model header ($95AC). $A544 turns $99 into the sine and cosine that $A4B2 uses.

Carry clear when the player is over the Colony Craft's pad: grid square 08-08 ($74 = $7A = 8), X and Y middle bytes $73 and $79 both $68-$77 (a square 4096 units a side), height middle byte $76 at least $FC; carry set otherwise. The height high byte is not checked. Callers: the deck landing ($A0E6), a grounded craft ($A01F) and walking ($A1DA), the last two only with the deck flag $FA set.

Per-pass movement, called by both main-loop branches ($859B, $85DE) just after $B2FE reads the stick. With the mirror flag $F1 set (toggled at $9353, a transporter) stick left and right are exchanged through $A17B, so turning matches the mirrored view. On foot ($A9 bit 7) or underground ($A8 non-zero): the walking model $A18B. Otherwise the vehicle's own model by JMP ($BEA0), the address $9D99 copies from the vehicle record: $9F17 flying craft, $9EFD ground vehicles, $9E5D space (to $AA62), $9EBE the fall from the Colony Craft, $9E66 then $9E60 the opening descent.
exchange left and right
$9F17 craft, $9EFD ground, $9E5D space, $9EBE fall, $9E66/$9E60 intro

Stick remap for the mirrored view, 16 bytes indexed by the joystick nibble in $80 (bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right; 0 = pushed): each entry is its index with bits 2 and 3 exchanged. Read only at $A16B, when $F1 is set.

Walking model: on foot anywhere, and in a vehicle while underground (turning only). During an elevator ride ($CA non-zero) the ride $A24A runs instead. On foot, stick up steps forward and down steps back ($A1ED with A = 1 or 0); left adds and right subtracts $AC to the heading $2D:$2C (16, set at start-up: 1/64 turn a pass). On the Colony Craft deck ($FA set), leaving the pad ($A13D carry set) starts the fall: vehicle 9 ($A9 = 9, record loaded by $9D99: the tumbling descent $9EBE), $A8 = 0. Then $A12B.
stick up: forward
stick down: back
stick left: heading + $AC
stick right: heading - $AC
walked off the Colony Craft: fall

One walking step: A = 1 forward, 0 back, flips the sign bit of the step length ($AA mantissa, $AB exponent: the float 80 set at $724D), so forward is -80. Y ($7A:$79:$78) += floor(step*cos heading), X ($74:$73:$72) += floor(step*sin heading), sign-extended: forward at heading 0 is north (Y falls), 256 west, 512 south, 768 east. Afterwards counts down $B1 (set to 2 at $8587 after an underground room change).

Elevator ride, run instead of any movement while $CA is non-zero (bit 7 set going down; the E key sets it at $B470). The panel interrupt ($BA7B, $BADD) runs the ride's clock: stage $CC (13 at the top) and fraction $CB ($00-$84). Height $76:$75 = 128*$CC + 64 + ($CB*221 >> 8), redone if $CB changed meanwhile, less 1792 when that is 1536 or more (the top stages sit around ground level), then -6 going down or +38 going up; $77 = 0 or $FF. Down on the surface, stage 8 enters room $CD (the lift's number, 1-8, set by the E key): $90BE with $08 = $CD and $09 = 7, colours $A5/$A6 from $C4/$C5, middle bytes $73 = $79 = 8, $A8 = 1, $FA = 0. Down underground, under height 128 the ride stops ($BB2F) at 128. Up underground, stage 12 comes out at the lift of square ($B4B6+$CD, $B4BE+$CD), middle bytes $71, low bytes 0, $A8 = 0, $CD = 0 ($950D, $9374, $B232). On the surface with $FA set (room 8's lift, at 08-08) the height is raised by $40FF00, to the Colony Craft deck.
going down?
underground, stage 12: out on the surface
surface, stage 8: into the complex
underground going down: stop at height 128
Colony Craft lift: +$40FF00

View matrix for the full transform $A75C; skipped when on foot with no elevator moving. With roll r ($28), pitch p ($2A), heading h ($2C) from $A544, applied to (X, height, Y) relative to the eye: x' row $40/$42/$44 = (cos r cos h + sin r sin p sin h, -sin r cos p, -cos r sin h + sin r sin p cos h), signs flipped by the mirror flag $F1; y' row $46/$48/$4A = (sin r cos h - cos r sin p sin h, cos r cos p, -(sin r sin h + cos r sin p cos h)); depth row $4C/$4E/$50 = (cos p sin h, sin p, cos p cos h). Projection centre $8E = 80 + round($8C*$42), $8F = 68 + round($8C*$48); $8C ($94E0) is height/4096 up to 16, so the centre climbs up to 16 pixels with altitude. Clip window relative to it, floats: $90 = -$8E, $92 = 159-$8E, $94 = -$8F, $96 = 135-$8F (the view is 160 by 136).
screen x of the centre
screen y of the centre

Turns the spinning vertices of the current location's building: each of the first $9F vertices (count from the model header, $959C) has its offset from the centre ($57A0/$57B0 X and $57C0/$57D0 Y, floats set at $960B-$9634, 64 units per model unit) rotated by the spin angle $99 (sin $9B, cos $9D): X = x cos - y sin, Y = x sin + y cos. The whole parts become the vertex's X low and middle ($0400, $0440 + $A0) and Y low and middle ($0500, $0540 + $A1). Called each surface pass ($85AA) and at start-up ($7280); does nothing when $9F is 0.

Trigonometry for the pass, from the 10-bit angles (1024 a turn) through $841F (sine) and $841E (cosine), all floats: roll $29:$28 gives sin $2E, cos $30, tan $32, cot $34; pitch $2B:$2A gives sin $36, cos $38, tan $3A; heading $2D:$2C gives sin $3C, cos $3E; spin $9A:$99 gives sin $9B, cos $9D. The table is offset half a unit, so sin 0 is 0.003. Called by both main-loop branches ($8566, $85A1); the tangents serve the horizon ($AFF7-$B04C).

Vertex $19 of the current location or room, relative to the eye, as floats for $A75C: X = ($0740:$0440:$0400) - ($74:$73:$72) into $52/$53, height = ($0780:$04C0:$0480) - ($77:$76:$75) into $54/$55, Y = ($07C0:$0540:$0500) - ($7A:$79:$78) into $56/$57; 24-bit differences converted by $8510. Called for every vertex by $96D8.

Next vertex of an object's model relative to the eye: reads three signed bytes (x, height, y) at ($1D) + $AD + 1, leaving $AD on the last; $A6AD orients them and makes 12-bit offsets (x16, +2048), which are added to the object's relative position $D5-$DD (lowered by 2048 per axis at $978A) giving floats $52/$53, $54/$55, $56/$57 for $A75C. Called by $97B5 for each vertex.

Centre of city square A (row*16 + column) relative to the eye, for the points $9054 projects: X = (column:$80:$00) - ($74:$73:$00) into $52/$53, Y = (row:$80:$00) - ($7A:$79:$00) into $56/$57, the eye's low bytes ignored. The height $54/$55 stays as the caller set it (at $905C: minus the eye height, times 8 by $9E93).

Orients and scales one model vertex (signed bytes: x $CF, height $D1, y $D3). For objects 0-15 ($AF) it rotates by the object's three angles (64 a turn) with $A728: $802A+obj in the x-y plane (about the vertical), then $801A+obj in the height-y plane, then $800A+obj in the x-height plane; an angle of 0 is skipped. Then each byte with bit 7 flipped (0-255 for -128..127), times 16, is an unsigned 12-bit offset: $D0:$CF, $D2:$D1, $D4:$D3.

Rotates the signed byte pair (X, Y) by angle A (64 a turn): $8434 puts 127*sin A in $BEBE and 127*cos A in $BEBF, $82D3 multiplies signed bytes (a*b/128); returns X = X cos - Y sin and Y = Y cos + X sin, at 127/128 of true size. Uses $0A-$0C.

Transforms and projects one vertex into slot $19; input: its position relative to the eye, floats $52 (X), $54 (height), $56 (Y). On foot or underground: the heading-only $A979. Otherwise, with $A320's matrix and inline log-table multiplies (as $82FA): depth z = row $4C/$4E/$50 into $5C/$5D, $6E = $80 if z is negative (behind); x' = row $40/$42/$44 into $58/$59; in front, x'/z into $5E/$5F and screen x $6A = $8E + round(x'/z * 2^($21/4)) ($21 = $18: times 64), $6E = 1 if that is outside 0-159 or overflows. y' = row $46/$48/$4A (from $A881), then the shared tail $A8E9.
$80 = behind the eye
off the 160 columns

Tail shared by both projections, y' in X/Y and $08/$09: doubled into $5A/$5B (multicolour pixels are twice as wide as they are tall); in front, 2y'/z into $60/$61 and screen y $6B = $8F + round(2y'/z * 2^($21/4)), bit 1 of $6E set if outside 0-135. Stores slot $19: flags $0700 = $6E (bit 7 behind, bit 0 x off, bit 1 y off); in front only, x'/z $0600/$03C0, 2y'/z $7600/$0640, screen x $0680, screen y $06C0; always x' $0100/$0140, 2y' $0180/$02C0, depth $0340/$0380, for the line clipper $99DD.
off the 136 lines

Heading-only projection for walking and underground (no pitch or roll), same slot $19 and outputs as $A75C: depth z = -(X sin h + Y cos h) into $5C/$5D, $6E = $80 if behind; x' = X cos h - Y sin h, sign flipped by $F1, into $58/$59; in front, x'/z into $5E/$5F and screen x $6A = $8E + round(x'/z * 2^($21/4)), $6E = 1 off 0-159; y' = -height, then JMP $A8E9. The brief's PC samples of play at $A9A0-$A9EF fall in its multiplies.

The escape into space: craft 7's per-pass handler (the interstellar ship; its descriptor at $9E1D points to JMP $AA62 at $9E5D, taken by JMP ($BEA0) at $A178). During an elevator ride ($CA non-zero) it runs $A24A, as the handler $9F17 shared by six other craft does. Before launch ($BEFE = 0) it only holds $2B, the pitch angle's quarter-turn byte, at 1. After script 7 pokes $BEFE = 1 (Y at PRESS Y TO LAUNCH, $1123) it never returns: shows the bitmap at $4000 ($C7 = $70) with no double buffering, applies colour step 0 ($AC26), marks the 21 stars for respawn (depth exponent byte 1, i.e. negative), clears the view to black ($B1A1 with A = 0) and runs the star loop for ever. A copy of the opening's starfield in the start-up code ($72FA-$74C9), without its deceleration and with the colour steps, the script and the keys added.

Escape starfield frame: one script operation ($8AB2: the ending's messages), joystick and keys ($B2FE, so CTRL+S saves and CTRL+Q restarts here), the colour countdown ($AC1C); waits for raster line 224, below the view; erases every star by zeroing the whole byte at its last position ($0400 x, $0480 y) in the bitmap at $4000, then plots each at its new position ($0680 x, $06C0 y) with ORA $5660,X (pair %01: the screen matrix's high nibble). Row and column addresses as in the line routines, with $40 in place of $25.

Moves each star, index in $19 from $AC4A down: last position := new; depth z ($0340 mantissa, $0380 exponent/sign) += speed ($AC4E/$AC4F, negative, $838B adds). If z is negative, or x / z or y / z (x at $0100/$0140, y at $0180/$02C0; $8334 divides, $8477 makes an integer) plus 80 is outside 0-159 or plus 68 outside 0-135, the star is respawned ($ABBD); else the screen position and z are stored. After the last star, once $BEFE is negative, the speed is multiplied by $AC50/$AC51 ($82FA) each pass until its exponent byte is $25.

New star, index $19: x and y are random 24-bit integers from $ADEF (high byte AND $AC4B minus $AC4C, so -$200000 to $1FFFFF) made floats by $8510; z gets a random mantissa and the exponent byte $AC4D (16384 to 32767). It is then projected at once ($AAF7), and respawned again until it lands in the view.
Escape starfield: star-loop passes left until the next colour step. $AC1C counts it down and reloads 3; it holds $60 at load, so the second step comes 96 passes after launch.
Escape starfield: offset of the next colour pair in $AC0C, 0 to $0E in steps of 2 ($AC40); applying the pair at $0E sets $BEFE to $FF, which starts the acceleration.

Escape starfield colour steps, 8 pairs. First byte to $A3 and $A4 ($60 or $00: the view background stays black); second byte (read at $AC0D) is the view's screen-matrix byte for $BB4F: star pairs %01 take the high nibble, $6 blue, then $B dark grey, then $C grey, brightening before the acceleration starts; %10 pairs black.
Second byte of each $AC0C pair, read as LDY $AC0D,X: the value $BB4F writes over the view's screen matrix ($60, $B0, $B0, $B0, $B0, $C0, $C0, $C0).
Escape starfield, once per star-loop pass: counts $AC0A down; at zero reloads it with 3 and applies the next colour pair (falls into $AC26).

Applies colour pair $AC0B of $AC0C: $A3 and $A4 := first byte (background), then $BB4F with Y := second byte fills the view's screen matrix with it and colour RAM with $A6. Advances $AC0B by 2, except after the last pair ($0E), where it sets $BEFE = $FF, which lets $AB97 accelerate the stars.
Escape starfield: index of the last star, $14 (21 stars, 0-20; also the count for the erase and plot loops).
Escape starfield: AND mask, $3F, for the high byte of a new star's random x and y ($ABCB, $ABE8).
Escape starfield: $20, subtracted from that masked high byte so that x and y centre on 0 ($ABCF, $ABEC).
Escape starfield: exponent byte of a new star's depth, $38 (2 to the 14th, positive): z is 16384-32767 with the random mantissa ($ABFF).
Escape starfield: the speed, a float added to every star's depth each pass: mantissa here, exponent and sign at $AC4F. $00/$15 at load is -32; rewritten at $ABAE as it accelerates.

Exponent/sign byte of the star speed (bit 0 sign, bits 2-7 exponent); the acceleration stops once it reads $25 ($AB9C): -32, then -129.5, then 1.2 % more a pass until exactly -512.0, 126 passes later.
Escape starfield: mantissa, $03, of the float the speed is multiplied by on each pass after the colour steps ($ABA0).
Exponent byte of that multiplier: $08 (times 4) for the first multiplication, so x4.05, then zeroed at $ABA8, so every later pass multiplies by 1 + 3/256.
Escape starfield: decremented and loaded on each accelerating pass ($ABB4, $ABB7), but nothing tests it; the intro copy's $74C9 is the same dead counter.
Octant 0 step: x + 1; the error $08 takes the slope $66 by ADC with the carry clear (CPX $6C found x below the end); on overflow y + 1, and y = 136 (off the bottom) ends the line.

Line drawing, octant 0 (right and down, |dx| >= |dy|). One of eight routines 47 bytes apart, entered by JMP ($0004) at $9D95 through $BC38/$BC40 with X = start x (0-159, multicolour pixels), Y = start y (0-135), $6C = end x ($6D = end y for the steep octants), $66 = slope (|minor| / |major| x 256; $FF for 45 degrees), $08 = $80 (error, half a step), $25 = page of the bitmap being drawn ($40 or $60). A pixel: ($02) = row start = $55D0,Y + 256 x ($5540,Y + $25), i.e. base + (y/8) x 320 + (y AND 7), plus 256 when x >= 128 (the carry of ASL x), and Y = $5700,X = (x/4) x 8 low byte picks the cell; that byte is ORed with $5660,X (pair %01) or ANDed with $7760,X (pair to %00), as $AE06 sets. Y is kept in $06. Plots first, stops after x = $6C, else steps at $AC53.
Octant 0's pixel instruction, ORA $5660,X (opcode $1D: pair := old OR %01) or AND $7760,X ($3D: pair := %00); the opcode is written at $AE1E.
Octant 0's mask-table page, the high byte of the pixel instruction's operand: $56 with ORA, $77 with AND (written at $AE06; the low byte stays $60).
Octant 1 step: y + 1; the error $08 takes the slope $66 by ADC with the carry clear (CPY $6D found y below the end); on overflow x + 1, and x = 160 (off the right) ends the line.
Line drawing, octant 1 (down and right, |dy| > |dx|): the same pixel code as $AC61; plots, and stops once the plotted y equals $6D, else steps at $AC82.
Octant 1's pixel instruction, ORA $5660,X (opcode $1D: pair := old OR %01) or AND $7760,X ($3D: pair := %00); the opcode is written at $AE21.
Octant 1's mask-table page, the high byte of the pixel instruction's operand: $56 with ORA, $77 with AND (written at $AE09; the low byte stays $60).
Octant 2 step: y + 1; the error $08 takes the slope $66 by ADC with the carry clear (y below the end); on overflow x - 1, and x = -1 (off the left) ends the line.
Line drawing, octant 2 (down and left, |dy| > |dx|): the same pixel code as $AC61; plots, and stops once the plotted y equals $6D, else steps at $ACB1.
Octant 2's pixel instruction, ORA $5660,X (opcode $1D: pair := old OR %01) or AND $7760,X ($3D: pair := %00); the opcode is written at $AE24.
Octant 2's mask-table page, the high byte of the pixel instruction's operand: $56 with ORA, $77 with AND (written at $AE0C; the low byte stays $60).
Octant 3 step: x - 1; the error $08 takes the slope $66 by SBC with the carry set (CPX $6C found x above the end), so exactly $66; on borrow y + 1, and y = 136 (off the bottom) ends the line.
Line drawing, octant 3 (left and down, |dx| >= |dy|): the same pixel code as $AC61; plots, and stops once the plotted x equals $6C, else steps at $ACE0.
Octant 3's pixel instruction, ORA $5660,X (opcode $1D: pair := old OR %01) or AND $7760,X ($3D: pair := %00); the opcode is written at $AE27.
Octant 3's mask-table page, the high byte of the pixel instruction's operand: $56 with ORA, $77 with AND (written at $AE0F; the low byte stays $60).
Octant 4 step: x - 1; the error $08 takes the slope $66 by SBC with the carry set (x above the end), exactly $66; on borrow y - 1, and y = -1 (off the top) ends the line.
Line drawing, octant 4 (left and up, |dx| >= |dy|): the same pixel code as $AC61; plots, and stops once the plotted x equals $6C, else steps at $AD0F.
Octant 4's pixel instruction, ORA $5660,X (opcode $1D: pair := old OR %01) or AND $7760,X ($3D: pair := %00); the opcode is written at $AE2A.
Octant 4's mask-table page, the high byte of the pixel instruction's operand: $56 with ORA, $77 with AND (written at $AE12; the low byte stays $60).

Octant 5 step: y - 1; the error $08 takes the slope $66 by ADC with the carry SET by CPY $6D (y above the end), so the error grows by $66 + 1 a step: a 1/256 bias no other octant has; on overflow x - 1, and x = -1 (off the left) ends the line.
Line drawing, octant 5 (up and left, |dy| > |dx|): the same pixel code as $AC61; plots, and stops once the plotted y equals $6D, else steps at $AD3E.
Octant 5's pixel instruction, ORA $5660,X (opcode $1D: pair := old OR %01) or AND $7760,X ($3D: pair := %00); the opcode is written at $AE2D.
Octant 5's mask-table page, the high byte of the pixel instruction's operand: $56 with ORA, $77 with AND (written at $AE15; the low byte stays $60).
Octant 6 step: y - 1; the error $08 takes the slope $66 by SBC with the carry set (y above the end), exactly $66; on borrow x + 1, and x = 160 (off the right) ends the line.
Line drawing, octant 6 (up and right, |dy| > |dx|): the same pixel code as $AC61; plots, and stops once the plotted y equals $6D, else steps at $AD6D.
Octant 6's pixel instruction, ORA $5660,X (opcode $1D: pair := old OR %01) or AND $7760,X ($3D: pair := %00); the opcode is written at $AE30.
Octant 6's mask-table page, the high byte of the pixel instruction's operand: $56 with ORA, $77 with AND (written at $AE18; the low byte stays $60).
Octant 7 step: x + 1; the error $08 takes the slope $66 by ADC with the carry clear (x below the end); on overflow y - 1, and y = -1 (off the top) ends the line.
Line drawing, octant 7 (right and up, |dx| >= |dy|): the same pixel code as $AC61; plots, and stops once the plotted x equals $6C, else steps at $AD9C.
Octant 7's pixel instruction, ORA $5660,X (opcode $1D: pair := old OR %01) or AND $7760,X ($3D: pair := %00); the opcode is written at $AE33.
Octant 7's mask-table page, the high byte of the pixel instruction's operand: $56 with ORA, $77 with AND (written at $AE1B; the low byte stays $60).

Plots one pixel at projected point X ($0680 x, $06C0 y) in the bitmap being drawn ($25), with AND $7760,X (pair to %00, the background colour, the colour of the white lines), unless the point's flag $0700,X is non-zero (not in view). Reached by JMP from $9787 with X = 0, after $A75C has projected a single point.

Random byte in A. The 16-bit shift register $F3:$E8 moves right one bit, its new top bit being bit 0 XOR bit 3 of $E8 (period 57,337 from the value at load). A returns the old $E8 mixed: bits 7-0 = e2, e1^e7, e0^e6, C^e5, e7^e4, e6^e3, e5^e2, e4^e1, bit 4 depending on the caller's carry. Callers: script op 10 ($8AE5) and 27 ($8D34), both starfields, $85F9-$860F, $910E, $B953.
Sets the eight line routines to AND $7760,X: a drawn pixel's pair becomes %00, the background colour $A3 (white on the surface, the wire-frame lines). Called at $8592, $85D5, $96F4.

Sets the eight line routines to ORA $5660,X: a drawn pixel's pair gets bit %01, so sky pairs (%01) do not change, ground pairs (%10) become %11, the colour-RAM colour $A6, and %00 becomes %01. Called at $858C, $9054, $96EB.
Writes A (the mask table's page, $56 or $77) and X (the opcode, $1D ORA abs,X or $3D AND abs,X) into the pixel instruction of all eight line routines ($AC76 to $ADC1, 47 bytes apart).

Display mode 'curtain from the top', split at raster line Y + 50 (Y = 0-$84). Patches the line-0 handler $B9BB to text mode ($B9C2 := $1B; $D016 stays multicolour) with $D018 from $F6 ($B9BD; $F6 holds $7E: the screen matrix $5C00 read as characters $6x, which are blank in the $7800 set), so everything above the split is a solid band of $A3; and the split handler $B9F8 to the bitmap ($B9FF := $3B) with $D018 from $C7 ($B9FA) and background $C6. Then places the split ($AE4B). Y >= $85 restores the normal view. Called by the wipes ($AEB3, $AF07, $AF14) and the elevator animation in the panel interrupt ($BAA9).

Places the split (also entered at $AEF0 and from the panel interrupt at $BAC5, when the handlers' operands are already set): Y >= $85 restores the normal view ($AE67); else the line-0 handler's raster line $B9DB := Y + $32 and its next vector $B9D1/$B9D6 := $B9E6 (18 NOPs, then the split handler at $B9F8), or $B9F8 itself when (Y + $32) AND 7 = 3 ($AE8B).

Normal display: the line-0 handler chains to the panel handler $BA1E at line $BA (186), and the mode operands go back (falls into $AE76): line 0 shows the bitmap, the split handler, now out of the chain, text.

Puts the handlers' mode operands back without touching the raster chain (also called at $BB29 by the elevator animation): line 0 bitmap ($B9BD := $C7, $B9C2 := $3B), split handler text ($B9FA := $F6, $B9FF := $1B). While the chain still passes through $B9F8, the view is the bitmap above the split and a blank band of $C6 below it: a curtain from the bottom.

The split falls on a line with (line AND 7) = 3, the vertical scroll that $D011 = $3B/$1B sets, where the VIC fetches a character row: the line-0 handler chains straight to $B9F8, without the 18-NOP delay at $B9E6 (the reason is inferred from the timing, not measured).

Curtain wipe that hides the old view, run by $AF6E before the flip when $C8 has bit 7 set ($94C4): hum ($AF3E), a 30-frame wait on $E2, then the band colour $A3 := the new place's ground colour $C4 while the view keeps the old $A3 as its background $C6, the higher hum ($AF3A), and the split descends 6 lines a frame from line 50 to 182 ($AE37). Then the new place's colours ($A3 := $C2, $A5 := $C4, $A6 := $C5) and $AED3.

End of both wipes: SID reset from $B921 ($B910); two sounds ($B958 with $1C, $B93A with $20) when a ground flash is pending ($F0); canned message $F7 printed when one is set ($8DAA); $C8 := 0 and the normal view ($AE4B with Y = $FF).

Curtain wipe that reveals the new view, run by $AF6E after the flip when $C8 is non-zero ($7F from $90E8 or $94C4): band colour $A3 := the old ground colour $A5, view background $C6 := $C2, new $A5/$A6 from $C4/$C5 and the colour matrix refreshed ($BB48); the curtain starts at line 182 and rises 4 lines a frame to line 50, with the hum ($AF3E); then $A3 := $C2, the higher hum ($AF3A), a 22-frame wait, and $AED3.
Higher hum of the wipes: SID $D401-$D40D from $AF61-$AF6D, the same set-up as $AF3E with voice 2 at $05E4 (about 89 Hz), then voice 2 gated.

Hum of the wipes: SID $D401-$D40D from $AF53-$AF5F (voice 2 at $0550, about 80 Hz, pulse width $800, sustain 10; voice 1 frequency high byte $09 and silent), then $D40B := $15: voice 2 triangle, ring-modulated by voice 1, gate on.

SID values for the wipes' hums, one byte per register $D401-$D40D: $AF53-$AF5F for $AF3E, $AF61-$AF6D for $AF3A (voice 2 frequency $0550, then $05E4). $AF52 and $AF60, the $D400 slots ($A8), are never copied.

Start of each pass's picture (main loop $8569 inside, $85AD on the surface; $90E3): $1A := $78, the row count for the sky fill; $02 := 0; waits for raster line 224, below the view; the closing wipe when $C8 bit 7 is set ($AE96); the buffer flip ($AF84); the opening wipe when $C8 is non-zero ($AEF3); the ground flash ($AFA8); view colours ($BB48) and panel ($B53D); then clears the new drawing buffer: inside ($A8 non-zero) to $AA ($B197), on the surface to sky and ground ($AFD5), after the black-flash countdown $F9 ($AFCA).

Double buffer: $24 counts passes. Even: draw into $4000 ($25 = $03 = $40) and show $6000 ($C7 = $78, which the line-0 handler copies to $D018); odd: draw into $6000 ($25 = $60) and show $4000 ($C7 = $70).

Ground flash: while $F0 counts down one a pass the ground colour $A5 is $BB7E + $F0; from 10 ($913F) dark grey, grey, light grey, three whites and back, from 31 ($936F) first 18 orange, purple, red, black; at 0 it returns to $C4.
Surface only: $F9, when non-zero, counts down one a pass and at 0 flashes the view black ($B242). Nothing traced writes $F9 by name; the zero-page swap at $B8F6 can.

Surface: fills the new buffer's view with sky and ground row by row, for a horizon at any roll. $82/$83 := $55/$AA (pairs %01 sky, %10 ground) and $84 := 0, or swapped with $84 := $FF when bit 1 of (pitch high byte $2B + 1) XOR (roll high byte $29), XOR bit 0 of $F1, is 1. The horizon's shift per row, |cot roll| x 128 ($34/$35; x 64 by the exponent, then x 2), goes to $7C:$7B (8.8 fixed point, multicolour pixels) and its sign, flipped by $F1, to $7D; $FFFE if too large. The crossing with the top row, x' = 80 + (33.5 x cot roll - h / sin roll) with h = tan pitch ($3A/$3B) x 2^($21/4), sign flipped by $F1: if 0-159, the split rows start at row 0 ($B0E1). The split's screen x is 159 - x'.

The horizon does not cross the top row: its crossing with the side edge, y = 68 + 2 x (h / cos roll + or - 79 x tan roll), sign from $7D. If 0-135, the 135 - y rows above it are filled whole ($83 when $7D is set, else $82; $B178) and the split rows start at the left edge (x' = 159) or the right (x' = 1). Otherwise $B0AA.
The horizon is outside the view: all 136 rows get one pattern ($B178 with X = $88): $83 when bit 0 of ((roll high byte $29 + 3) / 2) XOR $2B XOR $7D is 1, else $82.

Split rows: x' in $09, fraction in $08 (from 0). Each row: the cells left of the horizon's cell get $82 through the unrolled row fill in page $BE (entered at $BE00 + 4 x cell, $B10B), the cells right of it $83 through page $BD (entered at $BD00 + 160 - 4 x cell, $B0F9), each entry 2 later and $03 adjusted when it falls past the INC or DEC $03 inside those fills; the boundary byte, cell 39 - x'/4, is $BC4C + (x' AND 3) ($56, $5A, $6A, $AA: 3, 2, 1, 0 left pixels) XOR $84. Then $1A counts the row ($78-$FF, 136 rows), ($02) := the next row from $5558/$54C8,X ($55D0/$5540 by row) and x' moves by $7C:$7B (down when $7D is set); once outside 0-159, $B168.
Low byte of the JSR $BD00 at $B0FE, written at $B0F9: where the unrolled fill in page $BD starts, i.e. the first cell right of the horizon (4 bytes a cell, 6 at the INC $03 at $BD82).
Low byte of the JSR $BE00 at $B110, written at $B10B: where the unrolled right-to-left fill in page $BE starts, i.e. the first cell left of the horizon (6 bytes at the DEC $03 at $BE1E).
The horizon has left the view sideways: the remaining rows (0 - $1A of them) are filled whole, with $82 when $7D is set (the split had moved right) or $83.
Fills X whole view rows with A (kept in $06) through $BD00 (all 40 cells), advancing $1A and the row pointer ($02) from $5558/$54C8; nothing for X = 0.
Inside ($A8 non-zero): fills the drawing buffer's view with $AA, pair %10 everywhere, the room's colour $A5 (the matrix's low nibble); $B1A1 for $4000, $B1E7 for $6000, chosen by $25.

Fills $4000-$553F, the view part of the bitmap at $4000 (17 character rows of 320 bytes), with A; X must be $F8. 22 unrolled STA abs,X 248 bytes apart, the last starting 16 bytes early ($5448) so that the fill ends at $553F. Also used with A = 0 by the intro ($7313) and the escape starfield ($AA8F).
Fills $6000-$753F, the view part of the bitmap at $6000, with A, in the same way as $B1A1.
Flashes the view white (Y = $11 into $A3, $A6 and the screen matrix, $B244); called at $8970 just before SHIP DESTROYED.
The surface's colours become the next wipe's target: $B27D to $C2-$C5 (lines, unused, ground, colour RAM); sprite 0 light grey ($D027 = $0F). Called at $90D0, $A2BA and by $B270.
Flashes the view black (Y = 0 into $A3, $A6 and the screen matrix, $B244), when the countdown $F9 reaches 0 ($AFD2).

Flash body: $A3 := $A6 := Y and $BB4F fills the view's screen matrix and colour RAM with Y, so all four pixel colours are alike; sound $18 ($B958); waits for raster line 276 ($D011 bit 7, $D012 >= $14), then a delay loop of 6 x 256 x 256 turns (about two seconds); then the surface colours back ($B270, $BB48).
Surface colours from $B27D into $A3-$A6 (in use now) and, through $B232, $C2-$C5 (the next wipe's target). From the restart at $8127 (CTRL+Q) and after a flash.

The surface's four colours: $01 white (%00, background: the lines), $06 blue (to $A4 and $C3, which nothing reads by name: the sky is %01 = $6 from the ORA #$60 at $BB4C), $05 green (%10, the ground: $A5/$C4), $0B dark grey (%11, colour RAM: $A6/$C5). The start-up copy at $725B takes five bytes, the fifth ($A9) into $A7.

Keyboard scan (CIA 1: port A $DC00 drives the rows, port B $DC01 reads the columns, both set up here): the key number is row x 8 + column, the KERNAL's numbering; with several keys the last found wins (rows 0 to 7, columns 7 to 0). CTRL ($3A) sets bit 7 and either SHIFT ($0F, $34) bit 6 of $07 instead of counting as keys. No key, only modifiers, or DEL (number 0): $EA := $FF, carry set. Else $EA := the key, and $E9 := the key when its number differs from the previous scan's (a new press; $B4B2 resets $E9 to 4, meaning none); carry clear.

Joystick and keys, once per main-loop pass and per escape-starfield frame: $DC02 := 0 and $DC00 read as joystick port 2: bits 0-3 (up, down, left, right; 0 = pressed) to $80, bit 4 (fire, 0 = pressed) to $81. Any stick or fire input sets bit 7 of $BEC0 (script 0 clears it at $08BC and tests it at $0997-$0A14 before IS ANYBODY THERE and the other idle messages) and skips the keyboard; otherwise $B281 scans it, and a key sets the same bit and goes to the dispatch $B331.

Key actions (Y = new key $E9, X = held key $EA): CTRL+RETURN ($81) pauses, rescanning until another key is latched, which is then acted on; D ($12) drop ($98FE); L ($2A) leave ($B949, $98C8); - ($2B) and + ($28) act while held, multiplying the speed float $EC/$ED by $F8/$FC (0.98) or $08/$00 (1.03) each pass ($B499); CTRL+S ($8D) and CTRL+L ($AA) the save and load dialog ($B382); CTRL+Q ($BE) restart ($B3E5); E ($0E) the elevator ($B3FD); any other to $B47E (digits and SPACE through $BC50). Handled keys are cleared by $B4B2.

Save (CTRL+S: $825F := $8D) or load (CTRL+L: $825F := 0): sound ($B94D); prints SAVE NO. 0-9 ? ($3B) or LOAD NO. 0-9 ? ($3A) and waits for a key. A digit, $BC50 value / 2 - 4 with 10 meaning 0, goes to $825E as ASCII (after @0:MER at $8258); then PRESS RETURN WHEN READY ($38) and a wait for a key with $01 = $05 (banking unchanged, cassette bits cleared). RETURN ($01) goes to $819E, which saves or loads; any other key, or a non-digit before, prints the blank message $32 and resumes.
Waits for the message window to be idle ($E6 = 0), starts canned message X ($8DAA) and waits until the printer's frame count $E0 reaches 30, by which time the text has scrolled in.
A NOP (the target of the BNE at $B379), then CTRL+Q ($BE): sound ($B94D), clear the key ($B4B2), reset the stack to $FF, CLD and restart the situation at $80E8.
E ($0E) goes to $B3FD; every other key, still in Y, to the speed keys at $B47E (digits, SHIFT + digits, SPACE; anything not in $BC50 is ignored there).
E: clears the key ($B4B2) and runs on into the elevator code at $B400 (nothing while a ride runs, $CA).

E key, the test and the start of a ride (key_e_elevator at $B3FD runs on into it). Nothing while a ride runs ($CA non-zero). On the surface ($A8 = 0) the player must be landed ($7F non-zero, at any height) with both middle position bytes $73 and $79 in $70-$73 (the lift's centre is $71:00) on one of the eight squares of elevator_squares (X $74, Y $7A); at elevator 5 (03-15) the Pass must be carried (object $2E, bit 7 of $29EE), else canned message $39, PASS HOLDERS ONLY. Then beep, room $CD := the elevator's number 1-8, band colours $C6 := black (shaft_colour_13) and $C2 := dark grey (shaft_colour_12), and the ride down: stage $CC = 13, $CB = $83, $CA = $80. Underground ($B455) E works anywhere in a room numbered 8 or less (the elevator rooms are 1-8), in no other: $FA := $FF in room 8 (the Colony Craft's, so the ride ends on its deck) else 0, beep, $C2 := dark grey (shaft_colours), and the ride up: stage 0, $CB = $42, $CA = 1. Both start the hum (sound $30 on voice 2) and zero the speed (stop_craft).

Every key but E comes here (key_e_or_speed): the key number's low six bits index key_speed_values; 0 means not a speed key and nothing happens. Otherwise the set speed's exponent byte $ED := the value x 2 plus SHIFT (bit 6 of the key, the float's sign bit: reverse thrust) and its mantissa $EC := 0, a float of 2^5 for '1' up to 2^14 for '0' (each digit doubles it), or 2^-31, effectively zero, for SPACE and <- (the brake; SPACE is key 60, <- 57). CTRL is ignored, so CTRL + digit sets the speed too. Beeps on the surface in a vehicle (beep_surface_vehicle), then key_used.

+ and - (from $B35E and $B369, acting every pass while the key is held): multiplies the set speed $EC/$ED by the float in X/Y ($08/$00, about 1.03, for +; $F8/$FC, about 0.98, for -) through fp_mul, and keeps the product unless its exponent byte is $3C-$3F (2^15, just above the '0' setting); then the beep on the surface in a vehicle, and key_used.

Marks the newest key as dealt with: $E9 := 4, F1's number, which stands for 'no new key' (the save prompt waits while $E9 is 4, $B390), so the dispatch, the object keys T and B and script op 11 act on a press once. Called by every key action, script ops 11 and 28, object_loop ($9712) and the start-up ($7280).

Elevator squares, X (column) half: read as elevator_x + n for elevator n = 1-8 (the E key at $B41E, the arrival at the surface at $A2A6), so its entries are $B4B7-$B4BE (elevator_squares); the byte here is key_used's RTS and index 0 is never read.

The eight elevators' grid squares, X at $B4B7-$B4BE and Y at $B4BF-$B4C6 (read through elevator_x and elevator_y): 1 09-06, 2 09-05, 3 03-00, 4 11-13 ($0B-$0D), 5 03-15 (the Pass), 6 81-35 ($51-$23), 7 $88-$88 (-120,-120, shown as **-**), 8 08-08 (the Colony Craft's lift, used from its deck above 08-08). The number is also the complex's lift room ($CD) and the order of the E key's search, 8 down to 1.
Elevator squares, Y (row) half: read as elevator_y + n for n = 1-8 ($B425, $A2AB), so its entries are $B4BF-$B4C6; the byte here is elevator 8's X entry.

Colours Benson's message window: A into colour RAM $DB78-$DB8E (row 22, columns 8-30; the letters are holes in solid cells, so this is the window's colour) and into msg_colour_now. From panel_init_colours (red) and panel_update (red, or the Metal Detector's green or blue).
The message window's current colour, a variable after panel_msg_colour's RTS: panel_update compares its choice with it ($B565) and rewrites colour RAM only on a change.
Colours the EL dial: A into colour RAM of rows 19-22, columns 2-3 ($DAFA/$DAFB, $DB22/$DB23, $DB4A/$DB4B, $DB72/$DB73). From panel_init_colours (blue) and el_dial_quarter_colour.
Colours the COMP dial: A into colour RAM of rows 20-21, columns 34-37 ($DB42-$DB45 the tick row, $DB6A-$DB6D the letter strip). From panel_init_colours (red) and comp_quarter_colour.

Panel colours at every hardware setup ($8194): colour RAM of rows 17-24 ($DAA8-$DBE7) black, then the message window red (col_msg_window), the EL dial blue (col_el_dial), the COMP dial red (col_comp_dial), and row 19's figures: columns 8-12 LOC brown, 17-21 ALT purple, 26-30 SPEED green (col_loc_figures, col_alt_figures, col_speed_figures).

Panel readouts and engine note, once a main-loop pass ($AFC0); nothing during an elevator ride. (1) Message window colour: with the Metal Detector (object $1A, bit 7 of $29DA) carried on the surface ($CD = 0) in a city square other than 00-00 ($B7 non-zero) below height $10000 ($77 = 0), blue if bit 6 of the square's status $F2 is set, green if clear, red if bit 5 is set; red otherwise. (2) ALT, row 19 columns 17-21: $77 as two digits, then three digits of the fraction $76:$75 (alt_next_digit), so ALT = height x 1000 / 65536. (3) SPEED, row 19: column 26 '+' or '-' from bit 0 of $27, then fp_to_int16 of $26/$27: its high byte as two digits and its low byte x 25/64 as two more. (4) Engine noise on voice 2, on the surface except in motion mode $0A: sustain level (SR high nibble) = the speed's power of two less 3, at least 1 (0 below speed 1; reverse at 2^3 gives 0), release 8 ($C in reverse); frequency high = that level and the mantissa's top four bits (snd_engine_freq_hi, snd_engine_sr); the sound restarts when the level rises. (5) LOC from $74 and $7A (loc_coordinate).

Next decimal digit of a binary fraction, for ALT: X (high) and Y times 5/8, i.e. times 10/16 (the value plus a quarter of it, halved). Returns A = the result's high byte (a 16-bit input puts the digit in its high nibble, a 12-bit one gives the digit itself), X = A AND $0F and Y = the low byte, together the remaining fraction for the next call.

One LOC coordinate: the signed grid byte in X ($74 or $7A) as two digits at $5ED0 + Y (row 19). $EF := non-zero when it is 100 or more from 0 (X + 99 at least 199, unsigned). A negative value is shown as its magnitude with bit 7 set, the reverse figures. Past 99 the table bin_to_bcd holds $AA, printed '**' (glyph $0A is '*'); -128 reads $80BA, a code byte $A9, and shows a reversed '*9'.
Two decimal digits of X (0-99, through bin_to_bcd) into $5ED0 + Y and $5ED1 + Y (row 19 for Y = $30-$47), each ORed with $07 (bit 7 gives the reverse figures); Y advances by 2.

EL (elevation) dial, every frame from irq_panel except during a ride: the target is the pitch low byte $2A times 9/16 (0-$8F) in the quarter $2B; while the shown position $BB:$BA differs it moves one step the shorter way round: forwards here ($BA up, $8F wrapping to 0 into the next quarter, recoloured by el_dial_quarter_colour, $BC := 0 entering an even quarter), backwards at el_dial_back. A step scrolls the dial's glyphs (chars $FA-$FF, $7FD0-$7FFF: rows 19-22, columns 2-3) one pixel row, feeding in the marker $76E9-$76ED and, each time the 16-row strip wraps, the next scale byte from $768B + $BC.
Colours the EL dial for its quarter $BB (0-3) from el_dial_colours through panel_el_colour; returns C = bit 0 of the quarter.
EL dial colour by quarter of pitch, 0-3: 6 6 5 5, blue for quarters 0-1 and green for 2-3. On the ground the pitch is $200 ($A030), so the dial is green there, as the screenshots show.

EL dial, one step backwards (from el_dial_step when the target is behind): $BA down, 0 wrapping to $8F in the previous quarter (recoloured; $BC := $5B entering an odd quarter), and the glyphs scrolled the other way, the scale fed from $7682 + $BC.

COMP dial (compass), every frame from irq_panel except during a ride: the target is the heading low byte $2C times 9/16 in the quarter $2D; while the shown position $BF:$BE differs it moves one step the shorter way: backwards here ($BE down, 0 wrapping to $8F into the previous quarter, recoloured by comp_quarter_colour, $C0 := $B4 entering an odd quarter), forwards at comp_dial_forward. Backwards shifts rows 1-5 of the letter strip (chars $DB-$E0, $7ED8-$7F07: row 21, columns 34-37 show $DC-$DF) one pixel right, sets the tick row (row 20, columns 34-37) to char $F0 + (position - 2) AND 7, and every eighth step fills the left-hand char's column from the label text: $7684 + $C0/2 when $C0 is even, the marker $76E9-$76ED when odd.
Colours the COMP dial for its quarter $BF (0-3) from comp_colours through panel_comp_colour; returns C = bit 0 of the quarter.
COMP dial colour by quarter of heading, 0-3: 2 6 0 5 (red, blue, black, green). The start's heading $200 gives black, as in the screenshots.

COMP dial, one step forwards (from comp_dial_step): $BE up, $8F wrapping to 0 into the next quarter (recoloured; $C0 := 0 entering an even quarter); tick row char $F0 + (position AND 7); every eighth step writes the next label column into the right-hand char $E0 ($7F01-$7F05, from $768F + $C0/2, or the marker when $C0 is odd), then shifts rows 1-5 of the strip one pixel left.

Exchanges zero page $02-$FF with $BF02-$BFFF (zp_copy), so the game's page and the KERNAL's take turns there; clears $0780-$07BF (the vertices' height high bytes, which lie in the KERNAL's text screen at $0400); falls into sid_init. Called by hardware_setup ($813A: the game's own page, loaded with the file at $BF02, comes in), by save_or_load_game ($81A8) before the KERNAL runs, and by resume_game ($80BE) after it.

Loads all 25 SID registers $D400-$D418 from sid_init_values (the only writes of the volume $D418 = 15 and of the filter, off), then voice 3's control := $41, pulse with the gate on, so that message_tick sounds it by writing only its frequency ($D40F). From zp_swap and the end of the wipes ($AED3).

The 25 values sid_init copies to $D400-$D418: voice 1 $80 $00, pulse width $800, control 0, AD/SR 0; voice 2 the same; voice 3 frequency 0, pulse width $800, control $04, AD 0, SR $F0 (sustain 15); filter cutoff 0 0, resonance/routing 0; mode/volume $0F.

Starts sound A (an offset 0-$30 into the sound table snd_freq_hi) on SID voice 2 ($D407-$D40D, Y = 7) through the shared tail of sound_voice1; X and Y kept. Used for the elevator hum $30 ($B478), the engine $24 ($B61A), the transporter chime's second note $20 ($AEE1, at the end of a wipe while the flash $F0 runs), and the voice-2 releases $28 (start-up, $72F0) and $2C ($7469).
The key beep only on the surface ($A8 = 0) and in a vehicle ($A9 bit 7 clear), else nothing: for the speed keys ($B493, $B4AF).
The key beep only in a vehicle ($A9 bit 7 clear): for L ($B350), which leaves the vehicle.

The key beep: sound 0 on voice 1 (pulse, frequency high $59, AD $09, SR $09), then one extra step of random, so every beeped key press moves the random sequence on; A kept. For E, D, T and B ($98C5), CTRL+Q, CTRL+S and CTRL+L, the save number, and a script key test that matches (op 11, $8B6C).

Starts sound A on SID voice 1 ($D400-$D406): gate off, then frequency high, attack/decay, sustain/release and control from the four bytes at snd_freq_hi + A (sound_voice2 enters the same code at $B961 with Y = 7); the frequency low byte stays at sid_init's value; X and Y kept in sound_save_x/y. Sounds: 0 key beep, 4 building destroyed ($876E), 8 missile launched ($8882 yours, $8947 the attack ship's), $0C the attack ship's missile hits you ($8983), $10 your missile hits a ship ($884B), $14 walking into a wall ($9413), $18 the flash of a crash or a hit ($B24D), $1C the transporter chime ($AEDC, with $20 on voice 2).
X kept by sound_voice1 and sound_voice2 while they run (a variable after their RTS).
Y kept by sound_voice1 and sound_voice2 while they run.

Sound table, 13 entries of four bytes (frequency high, attack/decay, sustain/release, control), entry n at $B987 + n, n = 0, 4, ... $30: 0 key beep (pulse $59, 09 09); 4 building destroyed (noise $09, 0E 0A); 8 missile launch (noise $12, 09 09); $0C hit by the attack ship's missile (noise $06, 0B 0B); $10 ship hit (noise $16, 0B 0B); $14 wall (noise $04, 09 09); $18 crash or hit flash (noise $0E, 0B 0B); $1C and $20 the transporter chime, voices 1 and 2 (pulse $0E and $0F, CA 0A); $24 engine (noise $40, 00 F0; frequency and SR rewritten by panel_update); $28 and $2C noise with the gate off, which only lets voice 2 fade (release $C or $F); $30 elevator hum (pulse, 00 40; its frequency high set each frame from elevator_hum_pitch).
Sound table column 2, attack/decay, read as $B988 + n (the table's byte 1 of each entry).
Sound table column 3, sustain/release, read as $B989 + n.
Sound table column 4, the control byte ($41 pulse or $81 noise with the gate on; $80 noise with the gate off), read as $B98A + n; the bytes from here to $B9AA are the rest of entries 0-8.
Frequency high byte of sound $24, the engine: panel_update rewrites it every pass ($B604) along with voice 2's register $D408.
Sustain/release byte of sound $24, the engine: panel_update compares its new level with it ($B60B), stores it ($B610, and $D40D) and restarts the sound when it rises. Entries $28-$30 follow to $B9BA.

Raster interrupt at line 0, the view (vector set by hardware_setup and by irq_panel): $D018 from $C7 (the bitmap on show), $D011 := $3B (multicolour bitmap), background from $A3, $D016 := $18; then the IRQ vector := irq_panel and the raster compare := line $BA. The operands irq_view_d018_src, irq_view_d011, irq_view_next_lo/hi and irq_view_next_line are rewritten by view_curtain_top, view_split_line, view_mode_operands_normal and split_both_text, so that a wipe or the elevator ride can split the view at a moving line through irq_split.
Operand of irq_view's LDA for $D018: $C7 (the bitmap) normally, $F6 (the band's text screen) while the top band is text ($AE39, $BB39); $AE78 puts $C7 back.
irq_view's $D011 value: $3B (bitmap mode) normally, $1B (text mode) while the top band is text ($AE43, $BB41); $AE82 restores $3B.

Low byte of the handler irq_view chains to: $1E (irq_panel) normally ($AE69); $E6 (irq_split_delayed, $AE5E) or $F8 (irq_split, $AE8D, when the split line is a bad line, line AND 7 = 3) while the screen is split.
High byte of that handler: $BA for irq_panel ($AE6E), $B9 for the split handlers ($AE63, $AE92).
Raster line of the next interrupt: $BA (186, the panel) normally ($AE73), or the split line Y + $32 (lines $32-$B6) from view_split_line ($AE53).

Entry to the split handler when the split line is not a bad line: 18 NOPs (36 cycles) before irq_split, evidently to put its register writes at the same point of the line as on a bad line, where the video chip has taken the time instead. Reached only through the vector irq_view installs ($B9D1 := $E6).

Raster interrupt at the split line (only while a wipe or the elevator ride has moved it): $D018 from $F6, $D011 := $1B (text), background from $C6, then the IRQ vector := irq_panel at line $BA. Its operands (irq_split_d018_src, irq_split_d011) are exchanged with irq_view's so that either band can be the bitmap.
Operand of irq_split's LDA for $D018: $F6 normally ($AE7D, $BB3C), $C7 when the lower band is the bitmap ($AE3E).
irq_split's $D011 value: $1B (text) normally ($AE87, $BB44), $3B (bitmap) when the lower band is the view ($AE48).

Raster interrupt at line $BA (186), the panel: saves A, X, Y; IRQ vector := irq_view at line 0; text mode with the screen $5C00 and the charset $7800 ($D018 := $7E, $D011 := $1B), background white, $D016 := 8; message_tick while $E6 is set; then, with no ride ($CA = 0), the dials (comp_dial_step, el_dial_step), else one frame of the ride (elevator_ride_down for $CA bit 7, elevator_ride_up for 1); counts frames in $E2 to 50 and then seconds in $E3/$E4.

One frame of the ride down, from irq_panel: voice 2's frequency high := elevator_hum_pitch and the step := elevator_steps, both at 2 x stage + ($CB >= $42); $CB falls by the step and on passing 0 restarts at $84 with the stage $CC one lower. Stages 13-8: two text bands (split_both_text), the lower one taking the next shaft colour (col_msg_window + stage, $BBCA-$BBCE) at each stage, split at line $CB + $32, so the bands rise up the screen; stage 7: the room's view comes in below the split (view_curtain_top); stages 6-0: the whole view. elevator_ride ($A24A) lowers the height meanwhile, enters the complex at stage 8 and ends the ride at the floor (elevator_ride_end).

One frame of the ride up ($CA = 1): the same tables; $CB rises by the step and on reaching $84 restarts at 0 with the stage one higher. Stages 0-6: the room's view; at each later stage the upper band takes col_el_dial + stage ($BBCA-$BBCF) and the lower one the old upper colour: stage 7 lowers a band over the view from the top (view_curtain_top), stages 8-12 are two text bands, stage 13 puts the view's operands back (view_mode_operands_normal) so that the surface appears from the top; stage 14: elevator_ride_end. elevator_ride raises the height and puts the player on the elevator's square at stage 12.
Ends an elevator ride: $CA := 0 and voice 2's control := 0 (the hum off). From elevator_ride_up at stage 14 and from elevator_ride ($A302) when the ride down reaches the complex floor.

Makes both bands of a split screen plain text bands with $D018 := $F6 (the view's matrix read as blank characters, so each band is just its background, $A3 above and $C6 below: the elevator shaft); sets the operands of irq_view and irq_split.

View colours for the multicolour bitmap: matrix byte Y := $60 + ($A5 AND $0F), so pixel pairs %01 are blue (the sky) and %10 colour $A5 (the ground), then view_colours_y with colour RAM $A6 for %11; %00 is the background $A3 that irq_view sets each frame.

Fills the view's 17 rows, screen matrix $5C00-$5EA7 with Y and colour RAM $D800-$DAA7 with $A6, unless the first cell of each already holds them (resume_warm_start spoils $D800 on purpose to force the refill).

Transporter flash colours: ground_flash sets $A5 := flash_colours + $F0 as $F0 counts down from its start (never index 0): $0A gives $BB87-$BB7F, 0B 0C 0F 01 01 01 0F 0C 0B (grey to white and back); $1F (mirror_world) first reads 20 bytes on, into elevator_steps: 08 x 18 (orange), 04, 02, then 00 and the ramp.

Elevator ride: how many lines the split moves per frame, at 2 x stage + half (28 entries, stage 0 at the bottom): 02 04, then 08 through stage 11, then 05 03 02 01, so the ride starts and ends slowly. Also the start of the mirror room's flash (flash_colours).

Elevator ride: voice 2's frequency high byte (the hum), at 2 x stage + half: 02 x 4, 03 x 4, 04 x 5, 05 x 12, 04 03 02: low at the bottom, highest in the middle stages. $BBC1 (00) is beyond the last index.
Colour of the message window at start (2, red: panel_init_colours). Also the base of the ride down's shaft colours, col_msg_window + stage for stages 8-12 ($BBCA-$BBCE).
Colour of the EL dial at start (6, blue). Also the base of the ride up's shaft colours, col_el_dial + stage for stages 7-13 ($BBCA-$BBD0; stage 13's is replaced at once).
Colour of the LOC figures, row 19 columns 8-12 (9, brown).
Colour of the ALT figures, row 19 columns 17-21 (4, purple).
Colour of the SPEED figures, row 19 columns 26-30 (5, green).
Colour of the COMP dial at start (2, red). The two bytes after it, 02 08 at $BBC8-$BBC9, are read by no code found.
Elevator shaft band colours by ride stage 8-13, 0B 00 09 00 0B 00 (dark grey, black, brown, black, dark grey, black) at $BBCA-$BBCF; $BBCA is also the ride up's first colour $C2 ($B465).
Shaft colour of stage 12 (dark grey); also $C2 at the start of the ride down ($B448).
Shaft colour of stage 13 (black); also the lower band $C6 at the start of the ride down ($B443).

Line drawing: routine number by the line's direction code $67 (bit 0 dY negative, bit 1 dX negative, bit 2 steep): 00 07 03 04 01 06 02 05 ($9C12). The routine number indexes octant_lo/octant_hi, octant_clip_x/y and the clip tests.
octant_map + 1, which holds 7: the start-up's row-table builder borrows it as a mask (BIT $BBD1 at $72B3) to end each character row after eight pixel lines.
X of the screen corner a line heads for, by routine number: 9F 9F 00 00 00 00 9F 9F (column 159 or 0); $9C25 puts it in $6C, the end X, when the end point is off screen.
Y of that corner: 87 87 87 87 00 00 00 00 (row 135, the view's last line, or 0), into $6D ($9C2A).

Line clipping: 16 offsets (40 38 08 00 40 38 28 30 40 18 08 10 40 18 28 20) by an end point's region, 8 x the sign of its projected X (bit 0 of $5F or $63) + 4 x the sign of Y ($61 or $65) + its clip code ($6E or $6F, 0-3); ORed with the routine number and halved, it indexes clip_start_test or clip_end_test.

Line clipping, start point off screen: the screen edges the line can enter by (bit 0 right X = 159, 1 bottom Y = 135, 2 left X = 0, 3 top Y = 0), 32 entries; 0 means the line misses the view and is not drawn ($9C50).

Line clipping, end point ($9C76): 0 means nothing to draw. With the end on screen ($6F = 0) the index is $20-$23, past these 32 bytes into octant_lo ($BC38-$BC3B, 61 90 BF EE, all non-zero), so such a line always passes.

Line routines, low bytes of the split table with octant_hi: draw_line_octant_0-7 ($AC61 ... $ADAA, 47 bytes apart), by routine number; $9C17 puts the address in $04/$05 and $9D95 jumps through it. The first four also serve clip_end_test.
Line routines, high bytes: $AC x 4, $AD x 4.
The four pixel-pair masks of a multicolour byte, left to right: C0 30 0C 03 (the start-up's table builder, $72D2).
The byte where the horizon crosses a pixel row, by the crossing's pixel in the cell ($09 AND 3): 56 5A 6A AA, that is 3, 2, 1 or 0 pixels of %01 then %10, EORed with $84 (horizon_rows, $B122).

Speed value by key number 0-63 (row x 8 + column), 0 for all but twelve keys: '1' $0A, '2' $0C ... '9' $1A, '0' $1C (twice the digit plus 8, 0 counting as ten), SPACE and <- $42. key_speed_digit doubles it into the set speed's exponent byte; the save and load prompt ($B397) halves it and takes 4, giving the slot 0-9 (SPACE's 29 is refused).
Not read by any code found: $4C and 41 zeros, $BC90-$BCB9.

Leftover text in the Atari 8-bit's internal screen code (ASCII minus $20, the code the panel labels use), 40 characters a line: 'A. DISK DIRECTORY I. FORMAT DISK' then 'B. RUN CARTRIDGE J. DUPLICAT', cut off at $BCFF: the menu of Atari DOS 2, a fragment of an Atari's screen memory left in the image. Nothing reads it.

Unrolled fill of one bitmap row, left to right: cell j is at ($02) + 8j and $03 steps up one page at cell 32. Entered at $BD00 + 4k (k = 0-32) or $BD00 + 4k + 2 (k = 33-39, the caller doing the INC $03), it stores A into cells k to 39: 40 - k cells; $BDA2 (k = 40) is the RTS. fill_rows ($B17E) always enters at $BD00, all 40 cells; horizon_rows writes the JSR's low byte ($B0F9) with k = 40 - c to fill the c cells right of the horizon's cell with $83.
k=32: 8 cells, 32-39 (INC $03 here)
k=40: fills nothing (RTS)

Moving objects 8-15 (8 the player's missile, 14 the attack ship's missile, 15 the attack ship), table 1 of 10, the lifetime.
