The ten tables are read as label + object, so each table's bytes start 8 past its label: this one is $BDAB-$BDB2, and $BDA3-$BDAA are never read. 0 idle, $7F held; otherwise move_objects counts it down a pass and removes the object at 0. Set to 16 when you fire, 32 for the attack ship's missile, $AD for the attack ship, which fires only below $80.
Moving objects 8-15, X velocity low byte, added to $2880 + object a pass: bytes $BDB3-$BDBA (the eight here are shot_timer's).
X velocity middle byte, added to $2480 + object: bytes $BDBB-$BDC2.
X velocity high byte (0 or $FF, the sign), added to $2540 + object: bytes $BDC3-$BDCA.
Height velocity low byte, added to $28C0 + object: bytes $BDCB-$BDD2.
Height velocity middle byte, added to $24C0 + object: bytes $BDD3-$BDDA.
Height velocity high byte, added to $2580 + object (a height gone negative is set to -1, $FF:$FF:$FF): bytes $BDDB-$BDE2.
Y velocity low byte, added to $2900 + object: bytes $BDE3-$BDEA.
Y velocity middle byte, added to $2500 + object: bytes $BDEB-$BDF2.
Y velocity high byte, added to $25C0 + object: bytes $BDF3-$BDFA; $BDFB-$BDFF are not read. A save file holds $BDA0-$BDFF (save_state_table).

Unrolled fill of one bitmap row, right to left: entered at $BE00 + 4m (m = 0-7, with $03 one page up as fill_row_right leaves it) or $BE00 + 4m + 2 (m = 8-38, the caller doing the DEC $03), it stores A into cells 38 - m down to 0 of the row at ($02): 39 - m cells, stepping $03 down at cell 31; $BE9E (m = 39) is the RTS. horizon_rows writes the JSR's low byte ($B10B) with m = c, the cells left of the horizon's cell getting $82. $BE9F, a zero, is not read.
m=7: 32 cells, 31-0 (DEC $03 here)
m=30: 9 cells, 8-0
m=31: 8 cells, 7-0
m=32: 7 cells, 6-0
m=33: 6 cells, 5-0
m=34: 5 cells, 4-0
m=35: 4 cells, 3-0
m=36: 3 cells, 2-0
m=37: 2 cells, 1-0
m=38: 1 cell, 0
m=39: fills nothing (RTS)

The current motion record, 16 bytes copied by load_motion_record from motion_rec_0-10 ($9DAD + 16 x $A9); a save file holds $BEA0-$BEFF. Bytes 0-1, here, are the handler move_player jumps through (JMP ($BEA0), $A178): motion_flight $9F17, motion_ground $9EFD, motion_starship $9E5D, motion_fall $9EBE or motion_descent_1 $9E66, which rewrites the low byte to $60 at $9E8D (motion_descent_2, $9E60, as in play-ground-0808.vsf). Bytes 2-15 are that handler's constants; landing recopies bytes 2-11 from motion_rec_8_grounded ($A0CC).

Motion record byte 2, with byte 3 a float: motion_flight multiplies the turn rate $22/$23 by it each pass ($9F26), the turn kept when the stick is let go. motion_fall subtracts this byte from the height's middle byte a pass ($9EC1).
Motion record byte 3, exponent byte of mot_turn_keep ($9F29); motion_spin adds it to the roll $28 ($9ED9).

Motion record byte 4, with byte 5 a float: added to the turn rate while the stick is held left, and subtracted (its sign bit set by INY) while right ($9F39, $9F4C); motion_spin adds this byte to the pitch $2A ($9EE5).
Motion record byte 5, exponent byte of mot_turn_push ($9F3C, $9F4F); motion_spin adds it to the heading $2C ($9EF1).
Motion record byte 6: added to the pitch $2A:$2B while the stick is held up, subtracted while down ($9F63, $9F79); motion_ground sets it to 0 ($9EFF), so ground vehicles cannot pitch.

Motion record byte 7: exponent byte for the bank, roll $28/$29 := fp_to_int16 of the turn rate's mantissa with this added to its exponent ($A11B); a negative byte is used alone, giving no bank. Not while landed.
Motion record byte 8, with byte 9 a float: the climb, speed x sin(pitch), is multiplied by it before it moves the height ($A06B).

Motion record byte 9, exponent byte of mot_climb ($A047); climbing above mot_ceiling, 4 x (mot_ceiling - $77) is used instead, halving the climb for each unit of $77 above it, and $88 (no climb) from 64 above.
Motion record byte 10, with byte 11 a float: the speed $26/$27 becomes (speed + set speed x mot_thrust) x mot_drag each pass ($9FAF), so it closes on a steady value.
Motion record byte 11, exponent byte of mot_drag ($9FAC). Byte 12 ($BEAC) is read by no code found.
Motion record byte 13: the height high byte ($77) above which the climb is cut ($A04D); $5A instead in vehicle 1 with the POWERAMP (object $1C) carried.
Motion record byte 14, with byte 15 a float: the set speed $EC/$ED is multiplied by it ($9F9C) before it is added to the speed.
Motion record byte 15, exponent byte of mot_thrust ($9F9F). Also read as $BEAF + X by scatter_carried_objects ($862B, X from $EB + 1 down to 2), i.e. the carried list at $BEB1 on.

The carried objects, a stack read as carried_list + n for n = 1 to $EB: object numbers at $BEB1-$BEBA, ten at most. T pushes ($982D, refusing an eleventh at $9827), D pops the top one, the last taken ($990D); mirror_world reads it ($935D). Index 0, this byte, is never used.
carried_list's first slot, the object taken earliest; find_carried_object searches $BEB1 + 0 to $EB - 1 ($941F).

Count of Palyar sites destroyed: squares whose status ($2B00) has bits 6 and 5 clear (114 in the image). In building_hit_update, once the destroyed bit of the square hit has changed: +1 when it is now set ($87EB), -1 when the ANTI TIME BOMB has put a destroyed building back ($87E5). Then compared with sites_lost_mechanoid: a Mechanoid lead of 105 starts script 10 (the Palyars' reward: it puts the PASS, object $2E, in room 1, elevator 1's lift room at 09-06, the RED HANGER of its message), a Palyar lead of 106 script 26 (the Mechanoids').

Count of Mechanoid sites destroyed: squares whose status has bit 6 set and bit 5 clear (115 in the image): +1 at $87DD, -1 at $87D7 for a building the ANTI TIME BOMB restores; see sites_lost_palyar. Squares with bit 5 (27) count for neither. Both are saved with $BEA0-$BEFF.
The signed byte of script ops 22 (add the operand, saturating at +-127, $8D46) and 23 (test it, $8B03); nothing else reads or writes it. No script in the image uses op 22 or 23, so it stays 0.
Sine of the angle rotate_pair turns by (sincos64, $8437; a signed fraction, 64 steps a turn), read at $A72F and $A745.
Cosine of that angle (sincos64, $843E), read at $A739 and $A74F.

Script flags (ops 16 set, 17 clear, 18 test): bit 0 the last question was answered Y (the subroutine at $0AAB, used by buying and hiring); bit 1 the opposition-sites reward has been given (scripts 26 and 10); bit 2 the Hertz ship is hired (script 7 then needs no Novadrive); bit 3 set by script 37 when the author's advert is destroyed, tested by nothing; bit 5 the Brother-in-law annoyed (his Dart or house or new ship; the ending's 'IS PLEASED YOU'VE GONE'); bit 6 an event script is running (start_script sets it, each such script clears it); bit 7 the stick or a key was used (read_controls sets it, script 0's idle messages test it). $BEC1 after it is read by nothing found.

Script return stack: return positions (low, high) pushed at $BEC2 + $E5 by $8BC9 (op 4, and start_script for the script it interrupts) and pulled by $8BD2 (op 5). No limit is checked; the space runs to $BEF7. $BEC3 holds $4C at the hand-over, left from before.

Attack flag: script subroutines poke 1 after 'PALYAR SHIP ATTACKING' ($11BE) and 'MECHANOID SHIP ATTACK' ($11C9); attack_ship_update runs only while it is set; cleared when your missile hits the ship ($8850) or its missile hits you ($897E). Also the byte before location_word, where dictionary word $CB's pointer points.

Dictionary word $CB (pointer $BEF8): a location 'XX-YY' written by script op 15 when it sets $57ED ($8C05-$8C1E): the low nibble (X) as two digits at $BEF9-$BEFA, the dash $0D at $BEFB (never written), the high nibble (Y) at $BEFC-$BEFD with bit 7 on the last. Script 7 sets $57ED = $32 (02-03, the author's advert); no script or canned message prints word $CB.

Escape state: 0 on Targ; script 7 pokes 1 on launch ($1123, before 'THE AUTHOR SENDS YOU CONGRATULATIONS'), and the space handler at $AA62 then flies the ending's starfield for ever ($AA69); it sets $FF when its colour steps are done ($AC46), which $AB97 tests.

The hired ship (object 7): 0 none; script 2 pokes $FF at 'SHIP DESPATCHED' ($0EBA); $8634 then puts object 7 over 08-08 at height $7F:00:00 and sets $7F here, and lowers it by height/128 + 1 a pass until it stands on the ground, when this goes back to 0.

Swap area for the zero page (zp_swap exchanges $02-$FF with $BF02-$BFFF, read as $BF01 + X, X = 1-$FE, so $BF00-$BF01 are unused): whichever page is not in use lives here, the game's own as loaded with the file until hardware_setup, the KERNAL's in play, the game's again during a save or load. A save file holds $BF00-$BFFF, which is how a load brings back the game's zero page.

The game's restart_vec ($FD/$FE) while its zero page is parked here: JMP ($BFFD) at $8215, the way out of save_or_load_game after a save, a load or a failed load, jumps through it. It holds $2160 (SEI; JMP resume_game), which no code changes; after a load it is the file's copy.

CITY MODELS, $C000-$CF66 and $E000-$FFCF: one wire-frame model per grid location, reached only through the split table $2600 (low) / $2700 (high), indexed by location Y*16+X, and read only by $9575, which fills the vertex tables $0400-$057F (and $0740/$07C0 with the square's grid position) and the edge lists $0580/$05C0; $96D8 projects the vertices and $96E7 draws the edges. Format: +0 last vertex number; +1 last edge number; +2 pen split P, edges 0-P drawn by clearing pixel pairs to the background colour (the structure, seen against sky and ground), edges above P by setting %01 pixels, which show only on the ground fill (road marks), $FF all road marks; +3 rotor byte R, 0 none, else (R AND $0F)+1 turning vertices whose angle advances (R AND $F0)/2 a pass, with +4 and +5 the rotor centre x and z. Then the edges, one byte each (high nibble to low nibble, vertices 0-15) until a $00 byte, then two bytes each; vertices 60-63 are the far ends of the location's roads: 60 east ($2D00), 61 west ($2C00), 62 south ($2F00), 63 north ($2E00). Then the vertices: turning ones first, three bytes (dx, height, dz; signed quarter units round the rotor centre), then two bytes each: bits 0-5 of the first are x and of the second z (0 the west or north edge of the square, 63 the east or south edge, 1-62 the centre $80 -31..+30), height = bits 7-6 of the first times 4 plus bits 7-6 of the second; height 15 takes a third byte, 0-127 whole units, or with bit 7 set bits 6-4 units and bits 3-0 sixteenths. A unit is 1/256 of a grid square, the middle byte of a position. $00: edges 24-43 follow as byte pairs
vertices 0-28: x|height, z|height

Three bytes 4C 00 00 after city_sabins_cube ($CF25), the last model of the $C000 bank; unread, like the mark at $C4EB. A stale copy of object-model data follows.

149 bytes identical to $3F6A-$3FFE: the tail of the object model at $3F4A (used by objects $3D and $3E) and the whole object model at $3F8D (object $3F), in the format $9728 reads through $2800/$2840. The object table points only at the $3Fxx originals and no pointer of any kind reaches this copy, so it is never read. It is Novagen's, not the packer's: the original Novagen disk, booted to $5000, holds the same bytes at $C000-$CFFE. Why it is here is not known; a leftover from building the memory image is the likeliest reading. The last byte, $CFFF = $38, is the only one in $C000-$CFFF that differs from that disk, so it is probably the packer's (its run-length stage writes downward from $CFFF).
